  const enqueue = <T>(work: () => Promise<T>) => {
    const result = operations.catch(() => {}).then(work);
    operations = result;
    return result;
  };
  const inactive = (): Extract<SignIn, { ok: false }> => ({ ok: false, why: { code: "E_CLOSED", family: "client", message: "this app operation was superseded", site: "app.auth", rewrite: "await app.auth.login(email, password)" } });
  const hide = (state: AuthState = "signed-out", pause = true, why?: Refusal) => {
    if (pause) owner?.pause();
    const notifyHidden = [...scopes].map(scope => scope.fenceView?.());
    if (current !== owner?.view) void current.close();
    current = anonymous(why);
    signedOutOnline = onlineView(current);
    publish(closed ? "signed-out" : state, null, why);
    for (const notify of notifyHidden) notify?.();
  };
  // @ref LLP 3000.013#6 — a scope retains already-dispatched responses
  // through its local credential cleanup, including implicit retirement.
  async function cleanupScope<T>(scope: Scope, work: () => T | Promise<T>): Promise<T> {
    const capture = scope.cleanup ??= { depth: 0, finish() {} };
    // Preparation can schedule credential work before a Client exists. A
    // later task attaches its raw/custody owner to that same cleanup lifetime.
    if (scope.client && capture.client !== scope.client) {
      const prior = capture.finish, finish = holdClose(scope.client);
      capture.client = scope.client;
      capture.finish = () => { prior(); finish(); };
    }
    capture.depth++;
    try { return await work(); }
    finally {
      await scope.logout?.catch(() => {});
      await persistence.catch(() => {});
      if (--capture.depth === 0) {
        if (scope.cleanup === capture) delete scope.cleanup;
        capture.finish();
      }
    }
  }
  async function release() {
    const previous = owner;
    owner = undefined;
    if (!previous) return;
    await cleanupScope(previous, async () => {
      previous.pause();
      try { await previous.client.close(); }
      finally {
        if (previous.valid) try { await previous.save?.(); } catch (error) { report(error); }
        const retired = previous.client.session()?.token;
        previous.stop(); await persistence.catch(() => {}); previous.valid = false; scopes.delete(previous);
        if (retired) previous.issued.add(retired);
        for (const token of previous.issued) revokeRetired(token, { principal: previous.session.principal, epoch: previous.epoch });
      }
    });
  }
  function observeEpoch(epoch: string) {
    // A provisional owner does not replace the rollback candidate's duty to
    // observe the shared epoch. Fence every older scope before any callback.
    fenceScopes([...scopes].filter(scope => scope.valid && BigInt(epoch) > BigInt(scope.epoch)), new SessionEpochChanged());
  }
  function fence(scope: Scope, error: SessionEpochChanged) {
    fenceScopes([scope], error);
  }
  function fenceScopes(stale: Scope[], error: SessionEpochChanged) {
    for (const scope of stale) scope.valid = false;
    const affected = owner && stale.includes(owner) ? owner : undefined;
    const expected = revision;
    // Publish before raw retirement emits client callbacks, with every rollback
    // candidate already invalid. Auth and client observers share this boundary.
    if (affected && !closed) hide("restoring");
    for (const scope of stale) void cleanupScope(scope, () => {
      scope.pause(); scope.stop(); scope.aborter.abort();
      return scope.client?.signOut();
    }).catch(() => {});
    if (!affected || closed) return;
    void enqueue(async () => {
      if (owner !== affected) return;
      await release();
      if (revision === expected) publish("signed-out", null, error.why);
    }).catch(report);
  }
  async function open(session: Session, expected: number, epoch: string, restoring = false, openingSignOuts?: Record<string, number>): Promise<SignIn> {
    if (closed || revision !== expected) { revokeRetired(session.token); return inactive(); }
    const previous = owner, previousVisible = snapshot.state === "signed-in";
    hide("restoring", false);
    // Keep the prior runtime's rotations and pending-write custody alive until
    // commit. A failed replacement must not repair, revoke or detach it.
    // Every opener owns its persistence, including before it returns a Client.
    // Logout invalidates this guard synchronously, ahead of any network work.
    const scope: Scope = { valid: true, epoch, session, issued: new Set([session.token]), aborter: new AbortController(), stop() {}, pause() {} };
    const retire = (token: string) => revokeRetired(token, { principal: session.principal, epoch: scope.epoch });
    const cancelled = (): SignIn => {
      // A peer can fence this provisional scope before it becomes owner.
      // The still-current auth operation must finish cleanup/publication (or
      // retry restoration), rather than return with its view left restoring.
      if (!scope.valid && !closed && revision === expected) throw restoring ? new RestorationChanged() : new SessionEpochChanged();
      return inactive();
    };
    scopes.add(scope);
    if (options.device) refuseReadDevice(session);
    let restoreToken = restoring ? session.token : undefined;
    let preparing = true, committing = false;
    const scopedStore: SessionStore = {
      get: sessionStore.get,
      set: (key, value) => cleanupScope(scope, () => persist(() => storeLock(key, async () => {
        if (key !== custodyKey) { await storage.set(key, value); return; }
        const next = JSON.parse(value) as Session;
        const saved = await storage.get(key);
        let kept: Session | undefined;
        try { kept = saved ? JSON.parse(saved) : undefined; } catch {}
        if (!scope.valid || await readEpoch() !== epoch || (openingSignOuts &&
          (signOuts(saved)[session.principal] ?? 0) !== (openingSignOuts[session.principal] ?? 0))) {
          retire(next.token);
          const error = new SessionEpochChanged(); fence(scope, error);
          throw restoreToken !== undefined ? new RestorationChanged() : error;
        }
        if (restoreToken !== undefined && kept?.token !== restoreToken) {
          if (next.token !== scope.session.token && next.token !== kept?.token) retire(next.token);
          throw new RestorationChanged();
        }
        // Constructors can write/rotate several times. These saves are private
        // until their final successful opening; no durable account is displaced.
        if (preparing && !committing) { scope.session = next; return; }
        const replacing = preparing && !restoring;
        if (!replacing && kept?.token && kept.token !== scope.session.token && kept?.token !== next.token) {
          retire(next.token);
          const error = new SessionEpochChanged(); fence(scope, error);
          throw restoreToken !== undefined ? new RestorationChanged() : error;
        }
        if (replacing) await revocations.stage([...(kept?.token ? [kept.token] : []), ...revocations.pending()].filter(token => token !== next.token));
        const nextEpoch = replacing && kept?.token && kept.token !== next.token ? (BigInt(epoch) + 1n).toString() : epoch;
        // I2/I5: no separate epoch write and no fallible opening after this set.
        // Advancing the epoch already fences every opener that captured these
        // watermarks. Same-epoch rotations must keep their principal fences.
        if (kept?.token !== next.token || replacing || kept?.expiresAt !== next.expiresAt || kept?.capExpiresAt !== next.capExpiresAt) await storage.set(key, JSON.stringify({ ...next, snapback4Epoch: nextEpoch, snapback4Backend: url,
          ...(nextEpoch === epoch && Object.keys(signOuts(saved)).length ? { snapback4SignOuts: signOuts(saved) } : {}) }));
        lastOwned = { principal: next.principal, epoch: nextEpoch };
        epoch = nextEpoch; scope.epoch = nextEpoch; scope.session = next; scope.consumed = undefined;
        scope.issued.clear(); scope.issued.add(next.token);
        if (restoreToken !== undefined) restoreToken = next.token;
      }))),
      delete: key => scope.valid ? cleanupScope(scope, () => key === custodyKey ? removeSession(scope.session.token, restoreToken !== undefined) : sessionStore.delete(key)) : Promise.resolve(),
    };
    let pendingAuthority: Promise<boolean> | undefined;
    function authorized(): Promise<boolean> {
      // Memory/native session stores keep their original scheduling: their
      // persistence queue can contain an admitted write held by its owner.
      if (!authority || preparing) return checkAuthority();
      // Calls queued before this read starts share one linearization point.
      // Clear before acquiring the lock: calls arriving during/after the read
      // always queue a new committed transaction, including after peer logout.
      if (pendingAuthority) return pendingAuthority;
      return pendingAuthority = checkAuthority(() => { pendingAuthority = undefined; });
    }
    async function checkAuthority(start?: () => void): Promise<boolean> {
      const valid = await persist(() => {
        start?.();
        return storeLock(custodyKey, async () => {
          if (!scope.valid) return false;
          if (preparing || !authority) {
            if (await readEpoch() !== epoch) return false;
            if (preparing || !readOnly) return true;
            const bytes = await storage.get(custodyKey);
            const saved = bytes ? JSON.parse(bytes) as Session : undefined;
            return !!saved?.token && saved.principal === scope.session.principal;
          }
          const { marker, raw } = await authority.readScope(custodyKey);
          const stored = sessionEpoch(raw) ?? "0", legacy = marker ?? "0";
          const current = BigInt(legacy) > BigInt(stored) ? legacy : stored;
          observeEpoch(current);
          if (!scope.valid || current !== epoch) return false;
          if (!raw || logoutEpoch(raw) !== null) return false;
          try { return JSON.parse(raw)?.principal === scope.session.principal; } catch { return false; }
        });
      });
      if (!valid) { fence(scope, new SessionEpochChanged()); return false; }
      return true;
    }
    function admit(): Refusal | undefined {
      if (!options.device) {
        const refused = onlineWritesRefusal();
        if (refused) return refused;
      }
      const read = sessionReader(backing);
      if (!read) return admissionRefusal("the session store cannot be checked synchronously", "app.mutate", "use localStorageSessionStore() on the web, then retry with the same id");
      try {
        const marker = read(epochKey) ?? "0";
        const raw = read(custodyKey);
        const stored = sessionEpoch(raw) ?? "0";
        const currentEpoch = BigInt(marker) > BigInt(stored) ? marker : stored;
        // An unlocked observation may catch our own session commit before its
        // in-memory epoch assignment. Confirm under the lock before fencing.
        if (!scope.valid || !raw || logoutEpoch(raw) !== null || JSON.parse(raw)?.principal !== scope.session.principal || currentEpoch !== epoch) {
          void authorized().catch(() => {});
          return new SessionEpochChanged().why;
        }
      } catch (error) { return admissionRefusal(`session storage is unavailable: ${String(error)}`, "app.mutate"); }
      return undefined;
    }
    // @ref LLP 3000.013.000#3 — a device-less browser app journals writes when the
    // backend syncs no table, or when the app chose writes: "online".
    type WritesDecision = { mode: "journal" } | { mode: "synced"; tables: string[] } | { mode: "unknown"; why: string };
    let writesDecision: WritesDecision = { mode: "unknown", why: "the backend's schema has not been read" };
    let readingWrites: Promise<void> | undefined, lastWritesRead = 0;
    const journalSupport = !options.device && !readOnly && browserAdmission() && !!sessionReader(backing) && !!authority && !!globalThis.navigator?.locks;
    const readWrites = (): Promise<void> => readingWrites ??= (async () => {
      lastWritesRead = Date.now();
      let next: WritesDecision;
      try {
        const token = raw?.session()?.token ?? scope.session.token;
        const response = await scopedFetch(url + "/schema", { headers: { authorization: `Bearer ${token}` } });
        const json = await response.json() as { schema?: { tables?: Record<string, { sync?: unknown } | null> }; denied?: Refusal };
        const tables = json?.schema?.tables;
        const declaration = (table: unknown) => !!table && typeof table === "object" && !Array.isArray(table);
        // A malformed reply is an unknown decision, never "nothing syncs".
        if (!response.ok || !declaration(tables) || !Object.values(tables!).every(declaration)) next = { mode: "unknown", why: json?.denied?.message ?? `GET /schema answered ${response.status} without a table map` };
        else {
          const synced = Object.entries(tables!).filter(([, table]) => table?.sync).map(([name]) => name).sort();
          next = synced.length ? { mode: "synced", tables: synced } : { mode: "journal" };
        }
      } catch (error) { next = { mode: "unknown", why: String(error) }; }
      if (writesDecision.mode === "unknown") writesDecision = next;
    })().finally(() => { readingWrites = undefined; });
    function onlineWritesRefusal(): Refusal | undefined {
      if (!sessionReader(backing) || !authority) return admissionRefusal("this browser app has no device, and its session store is not localStorageSessionStore(): the browser write journal needs its synchronous reader and IndexedDB authority", "app.mutate", ONLINE_WRITE_FIX);
      if (!globalThis.navigator?.locks) return admissionRefusal("this browser has no Web Locks (navigator.locks); the browser write journal cannot serialize tabs", "app.mutate", "use a browser with Web Locks, or " + BROWSER_WRITE_FIX);
      if (writesDecision.mode === "synced") return admissionRefusal(`this schema syncs ${writesDecision.tables.join(", ")}; a browser app without a device journals writes only when no table syncs`, "app.mutate",
        `${BROWSER_WRITE_FIX} for offline reads, or createApp({ url, sessionStore: localStorageSessionStore(), writes: "online" }) to write through the server only`);
      if (writesDecision.mode === "unknown") {
        if (Date.now() - lastWritesRead >= 5_000) void readWrites().catch(() => {});
        return { ...admissionRefusal(`the backend has not said whether its tables sync, so the browser write journal is not chosen yet (${writesDecision.why})`, "app.mutate",
          'retry with the same id once the backend answers, or pass writes: "online"'), retryable: true };
      }
      return undefined;
    }
    const scopedRequest = async (input: Parameters<typeof fetch>[0], init?: Parameters<typeof fetch>[1], currentArm?: () => boolean): Promise<Response> => {
      // Cancel backend acquisition before a local Client exists. Once open,
      // the client owns cancellation and late rotation revocation itself.
      const path = new URL(typeof input === "string" || input instanceof URL ? input : input.url).pathname;
      if (path === new URL(url + "/auth/logout").pathname) {

  const signIn = (work: () => Promise<SignIn>): Promise<SignIn> => {
    if (closed) return Promise.resolve(inactive());

            // valid. Report the failure without announcing a logout.

    }
  });
  let closingApp: Promise<void> | undefined;
  function closeApp(): Promise<void> {
    if (closingApp) return closingApp;

      await release(); await current.close();
      await revocations.flushAcknowledged().catch(report);
      listeners.clear(); onlineListeners.clear();
    }).then(() => { for (const release of finish) release(); resolve(); },
      error => { for (const release of finish) release(); reject(error); });
    return closingApp;
  }
  return {
    auth, ready,
    get client() { return current; },
    get online() {
      if (owner?.view !== current) return signedOutOnline;
      if (!owner.online) owner.openOnline!();
      return owner.online!.online;
    },
    onOnlineChange(listener) { onlineListeners.add(listener); return () => { onlineListeners.delete(listener); }; },
    mutate: routeMutations((op, args) => current.mutate(op, args), (op, args, options) => current.mutate(op, args, options)),
    close: closeApp,
  };
}

codex
The frozen implementation checks retained `E_AUTH` responses against a rotation-specific floor at both capture and delivery. Plain sign-out leaves that floor unchanged. I’m tracing how ordinary and fallback requests use it, including successor adoption while persistence is still pending.

async function outcomeAuthFixture(t, tier, request, extra = {}) {
  const base = `https://outcome-auth-${++authFixtureSerial}.invalid`, queued = [], terminal = [];
  let settlements = 0;
  const backend = { generation: 1, schema: { tables: { remote: { columns: {}, indexes: {}, sync: null } } }, programs: [
    { name: "send", kind: "Mutation", args: {}, body: [] },
    { name: "remote", kind: "Query", runs: "server", args: {}, body: [{ table: "remote" }] },
  ] };
  const fetcher = async (input, init = {}) => {
    const path = new URL(input).pathname;
    if (path === "/schema") return Response.json(backend);
    if (path === "/probe") return Response.json({ ok: true, seq: 0, store_id: "kept-store" });
    if (path === "/sync") return Response.json({ snapshot: false, events: [], watermark: 0, more: false, generation: 1, acknowledged: [], store_id: "kept-store" });
    if (path === "/q/identify") return Response.json({ data: null, seq: 0, complete: true, store_id: "kept-store", tables: [] });
    if (path === "/changes") return new Promise((_, reject) => {
      const stop = () => reject(init.signal.reason);
      if (init.signal?.aborted) stop(); else init.signal?.addEventListener("abort", stop, { once: true });
    });
    if (path === "/auth/logout") return Response.json({ ok: true });
    return request(path, init);
  };
  const core = { async call(value) {
    switch (value.op) {
      case "engine_info": return { ok: { format: 1, version: "0.4.24", capabilities: ["sync-generation-v1"] } };
      case "sync_state": return { ok: { acquired: false, backend_required: false, store_id: "kept-store", watermark: 0, generation: 1, send_revision: 0, restore_watermark: 0, restore_images_at: 0, receipt_outcomes: true, outbox_status: true, adoption_capture: {}, pending_ids: queued.map(entry => entry.id) } };
      case "state": return { ok: { watermark: 0, generation: 1, native: null } };
      case "backend": return { ok: backend };
      case "next_submission": return { ok: 1 };
      case "meta": return { ok: 0 };
      case "apply": return { ok: { touched: [] } };
      case "admit": queued.push(value.entry); return { ok: value.entry };
      case "queued": return { ok: queued };
      case "query": return { ok: { loading: true, unknown: true, tables: ["remote"] } };
      case "begin_send": return { ok: { send_revision: 1 } };
      case "settle": settlements++; queued.splice(0, 1); return { ok: null };
      default: return { ok: true };
    }
  }, async close() {} };
  const options = { url: base, session: session("token-zero"), fetch: fetcher, waitSeconds: 1, ...extra };
  const client = tier === "local" ? await createLocalClient({ ...options, device: { open: async () => core } }) : createClient(options);
  t.after(() => client.close()); client.onWrite(write => terminal.push(write));
  if (tier === "online") await client.query({ kind: "query", name: "identify" }, {});

}

    if (++sends === 1) { entered = true; await held.promise; return authDenied("request from preceding revision"); }
    return Response.json({ state: "sent", id: ids.at(-1), seq: 1, store_id: "kept-store" });
  });
  const writing = effectCall(f.client, "mutation"); await until(() => entered);
  const refreshed = await f.client.refreshSession(); assert.equal(refreshed.ok, false); assert.equal(refreshed.why.retryable, true);
  held.resolve(); const result = await writing;
  assert.equal(result.state, "sent"); assert.equal(f.client.session()?.token, "token-zero");
  assert.ok(ids.length >= 2); assert.equal(new Set(ids).size, 1); assert.deepEqual(f.terminal.map(write => write.state), ["sent"]);
});

test("the default session store stays in memory and browser persistence is explicit", async () => {
  const calls = [];
  const values = new Map();
  const storage = {
    getItem(key) { calls.push(["get", key]); return values.get(key) ?? null; },
    setItem(key, value) { calls.push(["set", key, value]); values.set(key, value); },
    removeItem(key) { calls.push(["delete", key]); values.delete(key); },
  };
  const descriptor = Object.getOwnPropertyDescriptor(globalThis, "localStorage");
  Object.defineProperty(globalThis, "localStorage", { configurable: true, value: storage });
  const url = `https://memory-${Date.now()}.invalid`;
  try {
    await keepSession(url, session("memory-token"), defaultSessionStore);
    assert.equal((await restoreSession(url, defaultSessionStore)).token, "memory-token");
    await forgetSession(url, defaultSessionStore);
    assert.deepEqual(calls, [], "the secure default never consults page-readable localStorage");

    const persistent = localStorageSessionStore(storage);
    await keepSession(url, session("persistent-token"), persistent);
    assert.equal((await restoreSession(url, persistent)).token, "persistent-token");
    await forgetSession(url, persistent);
    assert.deepEqual(calls.map(([op]) => op), ["set", "get", "delete"]);
  } finally {
    if (descriptor) Object.defineProperty(globalThis, "localStorage", descriptor);
    else delete globalThis.localStorage;
  }
});

test("the local client rotates near expiry and keeps every protected request on the current bearer", async () => {
  const base = "https://sessions.invalid";
  const backend = {
    generation: 1,
    schema: { tables: { remote: { columns: {}, indexes: {}, sync: null } } },
    programs: [{ name: "remote", kind: "Query", runs: "server", args: {}, body: [{ table: "remote" }] }],
    native: { digest: "native-one", jobs: [], reads: [] },
  };
  const requests = [];
  let refreshes = 0;
  let native = null;
  let changes = 0;
  let answerOldPoll;
  const held = new Set();
  const doFetch = async (input, init = {}) => {
    const url = new URL(input);
    requests.push({ path: url.pathname, authorization: auth(init) });
    if (url.pathname === "/auth/refresh") {
      refreshes += 1;
      return Response.json({ session: session(`rotated-${refreshes}`, Date.now() + 7 * 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000) });
    }
    if (url.pathname === "/auth/logout-all") return Response.json({ ok: true, revoked: 3 });
    if (url.pathname === "/schema") return Response.json(backend);
    if (url.pathname === "/native.wasm") return new Response(new Uint8Array([0, 1, 2]));
    if (url.pathname === "/sync") return Response.json({ snapshot: false, events: [], watermark: 0, more: false, generation: 1, acknowledged: [] });
    if (url.pathname === "/q/remote") return Response.json({ data: "server", complete: true, seq: 0, tables: ["remote"], viewer: "user:alice" });
    if (url.pathname === "/changes") {
      changes += 1;
      if (changes === 1) return new Promise((resolve) => { answerOldPoll = () => resolve(Response.json({ denied: { code: "E_AUTH", family: "auth", message: "old token" } }, { status: 401 })); });
      return new Promise((resolve, reject) => {
        const stop = () => { held.delete(stop); reject(new DOMException("aborted", "AbortError")); };
        held.add(stop);
        init.signal?.addEventListener("abort", stop, { once: true });
      });
    }
    throw new Error(`unexpected request ${url.pathname}`);
  };
  const core = {
    async call(request) {
      switch (request.op) {
      case "engine_info": return { ok: {format:1,version:"0.4.24",capabilities:["sync-generation-v1"]} };
        case "sync_state": return { ok: { acquired: false, backend_required: false, store_id: null, watermark: 0, generation: 1, send_revision: 0, restore_watermark: 0, restore_images_at: 0, receipt_outcomes: true, outbox_status: true, adoption_capture: {}, pending_ids: [] } };
        case "state": return { ok: { watermark: 0, generation: 1, native } };
        case "backend": return { ok: backend };
        case "next_submission": return { ok: 1 };
        case "meta": return { ok: 0 };
        case "set_meta": return { ok: true };
        case "install_native": native = request.digest; return { ok: true };
        case "apply": return { ok: { touched: [] } };
        case "queued": return { ok: [] };
        case "query": return { ok: { loading: true, unknown: true, tables: ["remote"] } };
        default: return { ok: true };
      }
    },
    async close() {},
  };
  const store = memorySessionStore();
  const client = await createLocalClient({
    url: base,
    session: session("old-token", Date.now() + 1_000),
    sessionStore: store,
    device: { open: async () => core },
    fetch: doFetch,
    waitSeconds: 1,
  });
  assert.equal(client.session().token, "rotated-1", "a provided near-expiry session rotates before schema discovery");
  assert.equal((await restoreSession(base, store)).token, "rotated-1");
  await until(() => changes === 1, "the authenticated changes follower started");

  const observed = [];
  client.onSession((value) => observed.push(value?.token ?? null));
  const rotated = await client.refreshSession();
  assert.equal(rotated.ok, true);
  assert.equal(client.session().token, "rotated-2");
  assert.equal((await restoreSession(base, store)).token, "rotated-2");
  assert.deepEqual(observed, ["rotated-2"]);

  answerOldPoll();
  await until(() => changes >= 2, "the follower recovered with the replacement bearer");
  assert.equal(client.session().token, "rotated-2", "a delayed refusal for the invalidated token cannot end the replacement session");
  assert.equal((await client.query({ name: "remote" }, {})).data, "server");

  const revoked = await client.logoutAll();
  assert.deepEqual(revoked, { ok: true, revoked: 3 });
  assert.equal(client.session(), null);
  assert.equal(client.link(), "signed-out");
  assert.equal(await restoreSession(base, store), null);
  assert.deepEqual(observed, ["rotated-2", null]);

  const byPath = (path) => requests.filter((request) => request.path === path).map((request) => request.authorization);
  assert.deepEqual(byPath("/auth/refresh"), ["Bearer old-token", "Bearer rotated-1"]);
  for (const path of ["/schema", "/native.wasm"]) assert.deepEqual(byPath(path), ["Bearer rotated-1"]);
  assert.ok(byPath("/sync").includes("Bearer rotated-1"));
  assert.ok(byPath("/sync").includes("Bearer rotated-2"));
  assert.deepEqual(byPath("/changes").slice(0, 2), ["Bearer rotated-1", "Bearer rotated-2"]);
  assert.deepEqual(byPath("/q/remote"), ["Bearer rotated-2"]);
  assert.deepEqual(byPath("/auth/logout-all"), ["Bearer rotated-2"]);
  for (const stop of held) stop();
});

test("a stale-token mutation refusal remains durable and retries after rotation", async () => {
  const base = "https://rotating-write.invalid";
  const backend = {
    generation: 1,
    schema: { tables: {} },
    programs: [{ name: "send", kind: "Mutation", args: {}, body: [] }],
  };
  const queued = [];
  const oldReply = deferred();
  const newReply = deferred();
  const mutationBearers = [];
  let settlements = 0;
  let admittedId;
  const doFetch = async (input, init = {}) => {
    const path = new URL(input).pathname;
    if (path === "/schema") return Response.json(backend);
    if (path === "/sync") return Response.json({ snapshot: false, events: [], watermark: 0, more: false, generation: 1, acknowledged: [], store_id: "kept-store" });
    if (path === "/changes") return new Promise((_, reject) => init.signal?.addEventListener("abort", () => reject(init.signal.reason), { once: true }));
    if (path === "/auth/refresh") {
      assert.equal(auth(init), "Bearer token-zero");
      return Response.json({ session: session("token-one") });
    }
    if (path === "/m/send") {
      assert.equal(JSON.parse(init.body).store_id, "kept-store");
      mutationBearers.push(auth(init));
      if (mutationBearers.length === 1) {
        await oldReply.promise;
        return Response.json({ denied: { code: "E_AUTH", family: "auth", message: "rotated token" } }, { status: 401 });
      }
      await newReply.promise;
      return Response.json({ state: "sent", id: queued[0].id, seq: 9, result: { saved: true } });
    }
    throw new Error(`unexpected request ${path}`);
  };
  const core = {
    async call(request) {
      switch (request.op) {
      case "engine_info": return { ok: {format:1,version:"0.4.24",capabilities:["sync-generation-v1"]} };
        case "sync_state": return { ok: { acquired: false, backend_required: false, store_id: "kept-store", watermark: 0, generation: 1, send_revision: 0, restore_watermark: 0, restore_images_at: 0, receipt_outcomes: true, outbox_status: true, adoption_capture: {}, pending_ids: queued.map((entry) => entry.id) } };
        case "state": return { ok: { watermark: 0, generation: 1, native: null } };
        case "backend": return { ok: backend };
        case "next_submission": return { ok: 1 };
        case "meta": return { ok: 0 };
        case "set_meta": return { ok: true };
        case "apply": return { ok: { touched: [] } };
        case "admit": admittedId = request.entry.id; queued.push(request.entry); return { ok: request.entry };
        case "queued": return { ok: queued };
        case "query": return { ok: { loading: true, unknown: true, tables: ["remote"] } };
        case "begin_send": return { ok: { send_revision: 1 } };
        case "settle": settlements += 1; queued.splice(0, 1); return { ok: null };
        default: return { ok: true };
      }
    },
    async close() {},
  };
  const client = await createLocalClient({
    url: base,
    session: session("token-zero"),
    device: { open: async () => core },
    fetch: doFetch,
    waitSeconds: 1,
  });
  try {
    const terminal = [];
    client.onWrite((write) => terminal.push(write));
    const writing = client.mutate({ name: "send" }, { body: "once" });
    await until(() => mutationBearers.length === 1, "the old-bearer mutation did not enter the transport");
    const refreshing = client.refreshSession();
    await until(() => client.session()?.token === "token-one", "the replacement session did not become active");
    oldReply.resolve();
    assert.equal((await refreshing).ok, true);
    await until(() => mutationBearers.length === 2, "the stale refusal permanently dropped the durable write");
    assert.deepEqual(mutationBearers, ["Bearer token-zero", "Bearer token-one"]);
    assert.equal(queued.length, 1, "an obsolete refusal must not remove the outbox entry");
    assert.equal(settlements, 0, "an obsolete refusal must not settle the outbox entry");
    assert.deepEqual(terminal, [], "an obsolete refusal is not a terminal write outcome");
    newReply.resolve();
    assert.deepEqual(await writing, { state: "sent", id: admittedId, seq: 9, result: { saved: true } });
    assert.equal(queued.length, 0);
    assert.equal(settlements, 1);
    assert.equal(terminal.length, 1);
    assert.equal(terminal[0].state, "sent");
  } finally {
    await client.close();
  }
});

  const base = "https://rotating-watch.invalid";
  const backend = {
    generation: 1,
    schema: { tables: { remote: { columns: {}, indexes: {}, sync: null } } },
    programs: [{ name: "remote", kind: "Query", runs: "server", args: {}, body: [{ table: "remote" }] }],
  };
  const oldReply = deferred();
  const queryBearers = [];
  const doFetch = async (input, init = {}) => {
    const path = new URL(input).pathname;
    if (path === "/schema") return Response.json(backend);

    if (path === "/changes") return new Promise((_, reject) => init.signal?.addEventListener("abort", () => reject(init.signal.reason), { once: true }));
    if (path === "/auth/refresh") return Response.json({ session: session("token-one") });
    if (path === "/q/remote") {
      queryBearers.push(auth(init));
      if (queryBearers.length === 1) {
        await oldReply.promise;
        return Response.json({ denied: { code: "E_AUTH", family: "auth", message: "rotated token" } }, { status: 401 });
      }
      return Response.json({ data: "current", complete: true, seq: 0, tables: ["remote"], viewer: "user:alice" });
    }
    throw new Error(`unexpected request ${path}`);
  };
  const core = {
    async call(request) {
      switch (request.op) {
      case "engine_info": return { ok: {format:1,version:"0.4.24",capabilities:["sync-generation-v1"]} };
        case "sync_state": return { ok: { acquired: false, backend_required: false, store_id: null, watermark: 0, generation: 1, send_revision: 0, restore_watermark: 0, restore_images_at: 0, receipt_outcomes: true, outbox_status: true, adoption_capture: {}, pending_ids: [] } };
        case "state": return { ok: { watermark: 0, generation: 1, native: null } };
        case "backend": return { ok: backend };
        case "next_submission": return { ok: 1 };
        case "meta": return { ok: 0 };
        case "set_meta": return { ok: true };
        case "apply": return { ok: { touched: [] } };
        case "queued": return { ok: [] };
        case "query": return { ok: { loading: true, unknown: true, tables: ["remote"] } };
        default: return { ok: true };
      }
    },
    async close() {},
  };
  const client = await createLocalClient({
    url: base,
    session: session("token-zero"),
    device: { open: async () => core },
    fetch: doFetch,
    waitSeconds: 1,
  });
  try {
    const snapshots = [];
    const watch = client.observe({ name: "remote" }, {});
    const unsubscribe = watch.subscribe(() => snapshots.push(watch.getSnapshot()));
    await until(() => queryBearers.length === 1, "the old-bearer watch did not enter the transport");
    assert.equal((await client.refreshSession()).ok, true);
    assert.equal(client.session()?.token, "token-one");
    oldReply.resolve();
    await until(() => watch.getSnapshot().data === "current", "the watch remained denied after credential rotation");
    assert.equal(queryBearers[0], "Bearer token-zero");
    assert.ok(queryBearers.length >= 2);
    assert.ok(queryBearers.slice(1).every((bearer) => bearer === "Bearer token-one"));
    assert.equal(snapshots.some((snapshot) => snapshot.denied?.code === "E_AUTH"), false, "an obsolete refusal must not become the live snapshot");
    unsubscribe();
    watch.close();
  } finally {
    await client.close();
  }
});

test("a current-token sign-out cannot reclassify a stale write refusal", async () => {
  const base = "https://concurrent-signout.invalid";
  const backend = {
    generation: 1,
    schema: { tables: { remote: { columns: {}, indexes: {}, sync: null } } },
    programs: [
      { name: "send", kind: "Mutation", args: {}, body: [] },
      { name: "remote", kind: "Query", runs: "server", args: {}, body: [{ table: "remote" }] },
    ],
  };
  const queued = [];
  const oldReply = deferred();
  let oldMutationEntered = false;
  let settlements = 0;
  const doFetch = async (input, init = {}) => {
    const path = new URL(input).pathname;
    if (path === "/schema") return Response.json(backend);
    if (path === "/sync") return Response.json({ snapshot: false, events: [], watermark: 0, more: false, generation: 1, acknowledged: [], store_id: "kept-store" });
    if (path === "/changes") return new Promise((_, reject) => init.signal?.addEventListener("abort", () => reject(init.signal.reason), { once: true }));
    if (path === "/auth/refresh") {
      assert.equal(auth(init), "Bearer token-zero");
      return Response.json({ session: session("token-one") });
    }
    if (path === "/m/send") {
      assert.equal(JSON.parse(init.body).store_id, "kept-store");
      assert.equal(auth(init), "Bearer token-zero");
      oldMutationEntered = true;
      await oldReply.promise;
      return Response.json({ denied: { code: "E_AUTH", family: "auth", message: "rotated token" } }, { status: 401 });
    }
    if (path === "/q/remote") {
      assert.equal(auth(init), "Bearer token-one");
      return Response.json({ denied: { code: "E_AUTH", family: "auth", message: "current token revoked" } }, { status: 401 });
    }
    throw new Error(`unexpected request ${path}`);
  };
  const core = {
    async call(request) {
      switch (request.op) {
      case "engine_info": return { ok: {format:1,version:"0.4.24",capabilities:["sync-generation-v1"]} };
        case "sync_state": return { ok: { acquired: false, backend_required: false, store_id: "kept-store", watermark: 0, generation: 1, send_revision: 0, restore_watermark: 0, restore_images_at: 0, receipt_outcomes: true, outbox_status: true, adoption_capture: {}, pending_ids: queued.map((entry) => entry.id) } };
        case "state": return { ok: { watermark: 0, generation: 1, native: null } };
        case "backend": return { ok: backend };
        case "next_submission": return { ok: 1 };
        case "meta": return { ok: 0 };
        case "set_meta": return { ok: true };
        case "apply": return { ok: { touched: [] } };
        case "admit": queued.push(request.entry); return { ok: request.entry };
        case "queued": return { ok: queued };
        case "query": return { ok: { loading: true, unknown: true, tables: ["remote"] } };
        case "begin_send": return { ok: { send_revision: 1 } };
        case "settle": settlements += 1; queued.splice(0, 1); return { ok: null };
        default: return { ok: true };
      }
    },
    async close() {},
  };
  const client = await createLocalClient({
    url: base,
    session: session("token-zero"),
    device: { open: async () => core },
    fetch: doFetch,
    waitSeconds: 1,
  });
  let closed = false;
  try {
    const terminal = [];
    client.onWrite((write) => terminal.push(write));
    const writing = client.mutate({ name: "send" }, { body: "once" });
    await until(() => oldMutationEntered, "the old-bearer mutation did not enter the transport");
    const refreshing = client.refreshSession();
    await until(() => client.session()?.token === "token-one", "the replacement session did not become active");
    const refused = await client.query({ name: "remote" }, {});
    assert.equal(refused.denied?.code, "E_AUTH", "the current bearer refusal remains authoritative");
    assert.equal(client.session(), null);
    assert.equal(client.link(), "signed-out");
    oldReply.resolve();
    await refreshing;
    await client.close();
    closed = true;
    assert.equal(settlements, 0, "the stale response must not settle the durable outbox entry");
    assert.equal(queued.length, 1, "the stale write remains durable after concurrent sign-out");
    assert.deepEqual(terminal, []);
    assert.equal((await writing).state, "pending");
  } finally {
    oldReply.resolve();
    if (!closed) await client.close();
  }
});

test("worker, effect inspection, and service-session calls always carry the service bearer", async () => {

async function fixture(t, tier, cleanupAt = "device") {
  const { url, dir } = await server(t), cleanup = gate(), replies = [], releases = [];
  let armed = false, cleaning = false, deviceClosed = tier === "online";
  const underlying = tier === "online" ? undefined : tier === "wasm"
    ? webDevice({ wasm, persist: memoryPersistence() }) : processDevice({ binary, dir: join(dir, "device") });
  const device = underlying && { ...underlying, async open(...args) {
    const core = await underlying.open(...args);
    let outbox;
    return { ...core, onOutbox(listener) {
      outbox = listener; return core.onOutbox?.(listener) ?? (() => {});
    }, async call(request, ...rest) {
      const reply = await core.call(request, ...rest);
      if (armed && cleanupAt === "admission" && request.op === "admit") {
        cleaning = true;
        // A provider can announce committed outbox work before its admission
        // caller resumes (for example after independent journal recovery).
        outbox?.(request.entry.now, [reply.ok]);
        await cleanup.promise;
      }
      return reply;
    }, async close() {
      if (armed && cleanupAt === "device") { cleaning = true; await cleanup.promise; }
      await core.close(); deviceClosed = true;
    } };
  } };
  const memory = memorySessionStore();
  const sessionStore = { ...memory, async get(key) {
    if (armed && cleanupAt === "session" && key === sessionKey(url)) {
      assert.equal(deviceClosed, true, "public close has finished raw device cleanup before session cleanup starts");
      cleaning = true; await cleanup.promise;
    }
    return memory.get(key);
  } };
  const app = createApp({ url, device, sessionStore, fetch: async (input, init) => {
    if (!["/m/add", "/a/work"].includes(new URL(input).pathname)) return fetch(input, init);
    assert.equal(init.signal, undefined, "closing must detach the caller, never abort a committed effect");
    const request = JSON.parse(init.body), held = gate(); releases.push(held.release);
    const reply = { request, held, delivered: false }; replies.push(reply);
    await held.promise;
    const response = Response.json(reply.body), json = response.json.bind(response);
    response.json = async () => { const body = await json(); reply.delivered = true; return body; };
    return response;
  } });
  t.after(async () => { armed = false; cleanup.release(); for (const release of releases) release(); await app.close(); });
  await app.ready; assert.equal((await app.auth.guest()).ok, true);
  return { app, replies, cleanup, arm() { armed = true; }, cleaning: () => cleaning };
}

for (const tier of ["wasm", "native"]) test(`${tier}: a dispatched body stays known when close overtakes the admission continuation`, { timeout: hangBudget(12) }, async t => {
  const f = await fixture(t, tier, "admission"), id = mintId();
  f.arm(); const writing = f.app.mutate(mutation, { body: "admission still returning" }, { id });
  await until(() => f.cleaning() && f.replies.length === 1);
  const sent = { state: "sent", id, seq: 7, result: { answer: "known during admission" } };
  f.replies[0].body = sent; f.replies[0].held.release();
  await until(() => f.replies[0].delivered);
  const closing = f.app.close(); f.cleanup.release();
  await closing; assert.deepEqual(await writing, sent);
});

for (const tier of ["online", "wasm", "native"]) for (const kind of ["mutation", "action"]) for (const different of [false, true]) {
  test(`${tier} ${kind}: concurrent same-id calls with ${different ? "different" : "identical"} arguments keep their own cleanup outcomes`, { timeout: hangBudget(12) }, async t => {
    const f = await fixture(t, tier, tier === "online" ? "session" : "device"), id = mintId(), args = { body: "first" };
    const call = args => kind === "mutation" ? f.app.mutate(mutation, args, { id }) : f.app.client.act(action, args, { id });
    const first = call(args); await until(() => f.replies.length === 1);
    const second = call(different ? { body: "second" } : args);
    // Mutations coalesce identical invocations and reject conflicting input
    // before dispatch. Actions have one transport response per invocation.
    if (kind === "mutation" && different) assert.equal((await second).why.code, "E_WRITE_ID_REUSE");
    if (kind === "action") await until(() => f.replies.length === 2);
    await new Promise(resolve => setImmediate(resolve));
    f.arm(); const closing = f.app.close(); await until(f.cleaning);
    const success = kind === "mutation" ? { state: "sent", id, seq: 7, result: { answer: "first" } }
      : { state: "done", id, result: { answer: "first" } };
    f.replies[0].body = success;
    if (kind === "action") {
      f.replies[1].body = different ? { state: "failed", id, why } : success;
      // Deliver in reverse invocation order. ID-keyed capture swaps outcomes.
      f.replies[1].held.release(); await until(() => f.replies[1].delivered);
    }
    f.replies[0].held.release(); await until(() => f.replies[0].delivered);
    f.cleanup.release(); await closing;
    assert.deepEqual(await first, success);
    if (kind === "action") assert.deepEqual(await second, different ? { state: "failed", id, why } : success);
    else if (!different) assert.deepEqual(await second, success, "overlapping mutation callers share the full outcome");
    assert.equal(f.replies.length, kind === "mutation" ? 1 : 2);
  });
}

for (const tier of ["online", "wasm", "native"]) for (const known of [false, true]) {
  test(`${tier}: overlapping mutation callers share ${known ? "a refusal" : "pending"} across close`, { timeout: hangBudget(9) }, async t => {
    const f = await fixture(t, tier, "session"), id = mintId(), args = { body: "same" };
    const first = f.app.mutate(mutation, args, { id }); await until(() => f.replies.length === 1);
    const second = f.app.mutate(mutation, args, { id });
    // Enter both submissions before hiding the facade (its authorization
    // check is asynchronous); neither caller is a later receipt lookup.
    await new Promise(resolve => setImmediate(resolve));
    f.arm(); const closing = f.app.close(); await until(f.cleaning);
    const failed = { state: "failed", id, why }; f.replies[0].body = failed;
    if (known) { f.replies[0].held.release(); await until(() => f.replies[0].delivered); }
    f.cleanup.release(); await closing;
    const expected = known ? failed : { state: "pending", id };
    assert.deepEqual(await first, expected); assert.deepEqual(await second, expected);
    f.replies[0].held.release(); await until(() => f.replies[0].delivered);
    assert.equal(f.replies.length, 1);
  });
}

for (const tier of ["online", "wasm", "native"]) for (const kind of ["mutation", "action"]) for (const failed of [false, true]) {
  test(`${tier} ${kind}: ${failed ? "refusal" : "success"} arriving during app session cleanup reaches its caller`, { timeout: hangBudget(6) }, async t => {
    const f = await fixture(t, tier, "session"), id = mintId();
    const pending = kind === "mutation" ? f.app.mutate(mutation, { body: "one" }, { id }) : f.app.client.act(action, {}, { id });
    await until(() => f.replies.length === 1);
    f.arm(); const closing = f.app.close(); await until(f.cleaning);
    const expected = failed ? { state: "failed", id, why } : kind === "mutation"
      ? { state: "sent", id, seq: 9, result: "known" } : { state: "done", id, result: "known" };
    f.replies[0].body = expected; f.replies[0].held.release(); await until(() => f.replies[0].delivered);
    f.cleanup.release(); await closing;
    assert.deepEqual(await pending, expected);
  });
}

for (const tier of ["online", "wasm", "native"]) for (const queuedGlobal of [false, true]) test(`${tier}: public close detaches a held refresh and retires its late successor; queued global logout=${queuedGlobal}`, { timeout: hangBudget(18) }, async t => {
  const { url, dir } = await server(t), held = gate(); let successor, consumed = false;
  const device = tier === "online" ? undefined : tier === "wasm" ? webDevice({ wasm, persist: memoryPersistence() }) : processDevice({ binary, dir: join(dir, "device") });
  const app = createApp({ url, device, sessionStore: memorySessionStore(), fetch: async (input, init) => {
    if (new URL(input).pathname !== "/auth/refresh") return fetch(input, init);
    assert.equal(init.signal, undefined);
    const body = await (await fetch(input, init)).json(); successor = body.session;
    await held.promise;
    const response = Response.json(body), json = response.json.bind(response);
    response.json = async () => { const body = await json(); consumed = true; return body; };
    return response;
  } });
  t.after(async () => { held.release(); await app.close(); });
  await app.ready; assert.equal((await app.auth.guest()).ok, true);
  const refresh = app.client.refreshSession(); await until(() => successor);
  const revoking = queuedGlobal ? app.auth.logoutEverywhere() : undefined;
  await new Promise(resolve => setImmediate(resolve));
  let closed = false;
  const closing = app.close().then(() => { closed = true; });
  await until(() => closed, "close must complete without releasing the held refresh");
  await closing; assert.equal((await refresh).ok, false);
  if (revoking) assert.equal((await revoking).ok, false);
  held.release(); await until(() => consumed);
  await until(async () => {
    const reply = await fetch(`${url}/q/list`, { method: "POST", headers: { authorization: `Bearer ${successor.token}`, "content-type": "application/json" }, body: '{"args":{}}' });
    return (await reply.json()).denied?.code === "E_AUTH";
  }, "the late unkept successor is rejected by the server");
});

for (const tier of ["wasm", "native"]) test(`${tier}: raw close finishes already-started rotation persistence and keeps that successor`, { timeout: hangBudget(14) }, async t => {
  const { url, dir } = await server(t), held = gate(), memory = memorySessionStore();
  let armed = false, saving = false, deviceClosed = false;
  const underlying = tier === "wasm" ? webDevice({ wasm, persist: memoryPersistence() }) : processDevice({ binary, dir: join(dir, "device") });
  const device = { ...underlying, async open(...args) {
    const core = await underlying.open(...args);
    return { ...core, async close() { deviceClosed = true; await core.close(); } };
  } };
  const client = await createLocalClient({ url, device, guest: true, sessionStore: { ...memory, async set(key, value) {
    if (armed && key === sessionKey(url)) { saving = true; await held.promise; }
    await memory.set(key, value);
  } } });
  t.after(async () => { held.release(); await client.close(); });
  armed = true;
  const refreshing = client.refreshSession(); await until(() => saving);
  const successor = client.session(); let closed = false;
  const closing = client.close().then(() => { closed = true; });
  await new Promise(resolve => setImmediate(resolve));
  assert.equal(closed, false); assert.equal(deviceClosed, false, "device cleanup cannot overtake an already-started session save");
  held.release(); await closing;
  assert.equal((await refreshing).ok, true);
  assert.deepEqual(JSON.parse(await memory.get(sessionKey(url))), successor);
  const response = await fetch(`${url}/q/list`, { method: "POST", headers: { authorization: `Bearer ${successor.token}`, "content-type": "application/json" }, body: '{"args":{}}' });
  assert.deepEqual((await response.json()).data, [], "close keeps the successor whose persistence had already started");
});

for (const tier of ["online", "wasm", "native"]) test(`${tier}: public close detaches held global revocation but keeps its acknowledgement custody`, { timeout: hangBudget(16) }, async t => {
  const { url, dir } = await server(t), held = gate(), sessions = memorySessionStore();
  let received, consumed = false, attempts = 0;
  const device = tier === "online" ? undefined : tier === "wasm" ? webDevice({ wasm, persist: memoryPersistence() }) : processDevice({ binary, dir: join(dir, "device") });
  const options = { url, device, sessionStore: sessions, fetch: async (input, init) => {
    if (new URL(input).pathname !== "/auth/logout-all") return fetch(input, init);
    attempts++;
    assert.equal(init.signal, undefined);
    received = await (await fetch(input, init)).json();
    await held.promise;
    const response = Response.json(received), json = response.json.bind(response);
    response.json = async () => { const body = await json(); consumed = true; return body; };
    return response;
  } };
  const app = createApp(options);
  t.after(async () => { held.release(); await app.close(); });
  await app.ready; assert.equal((await app.auth.guest()).ok, true);
  const revoking = app.auth.logoutEverywhere(); await until(() => received);
  assert.equal(received.ok, true, "global revocation committed before its body was held");
  let closed = false;
  const closing = app.close().then(() => { closed = true; });
  await until(() => closed, "close cannot queue behind unread global revocation");
  await closing; assert.equal((await revoking).ok, false);
  held.release(); await until(() => consumed);
  await until(async () => {
    const journal = JSON.parse(await sessions.get(sessionKey(url) + ".revocations") ?? "null");
    return !journal?.all?.length;
  }, "the detached request persists its acknowledgement");
  const reopened = createApp(options); t.after(() => reopened.close()); await reopened.ready;
  assert.equal(reopened.auth.state, "signed-out");
  assert.equal(attempts, 1, "reopening never reconsumes an acknowledged global bearer");
});

# LLP 3000.000.000.001: Staging with real users

**Type:** RFC
**Status:** Implemented
**Systems:** Snapback 4 deployment, password identity, development doors, proof kit
**Author:** Codex for Charlie Cheever (STAGE)
**Date:** 2026-10-18
**Revised:** 2026-10-22 (DX6 §11); 2026-10-21 (DX5 §10); 2026-10-19 (DX4 §§8–9); 2026-10-18
**Related:** [Release activation](./3000.000.000-retained-storage-and-hot-release.rfc.md), [Proof kit](./3000.011.003.000.000-packaged-proof-kit.rfc.md), [Store ownership](./3000.019-what-the-builder-still-wrote.rfc.md#34-p8-residency-you-can-see-and-a-cli-that-does-not-fight-the-dev-server)

## 1. Commission and boundary

Implementer: STAGE, 2026-10-18, commissioned by Charlie's wave-16 bakeoff
fixes #1/#4. Ten Muse probes used dev because password-role provisioning
had no single recipe. This amendment supplies that recipe using the existing
signup and service-seat authority. No system seed door is added to serve.
SEC owns self-promotion lints and security invariants; KIT4 owns unrelated
proof helpers, PROD2 owns production starter adaptation.

`deploy <dir> --staging` classifies a **new deployment store**, under its
exclusive owner, with durable metadata `deployment_environment=staging`.
An existing store with no classification is production, including legacy stores;
it cannot be relabelled. A staging store remains staging through deploy,
rollback, restart, copying and source edits. There is no promote/relabel flag:
production requires a separate fresh deployment without --staging and real
operator provisioning. --check never creates the classification. Repeating
--staging on an already staging store is allowed, including while serve runs;
it verifies the existing classification without changing it. Malicious edits by
the filesystem/database owner are outside the threat model, as for service tokens.
This is a deployment-lifetime boundary stronger than a mutable per-release flag:
production source or a seed plan cannot opt a production store into test setup.

## 2. Real staging accounts

`GET /auth/config` reports `development` independently of door availability,
`devDoors`, and `environment` (`development`, `staging`, or `production`).
Missing/unknown environment metadata is production. serve remains bearer-only
in both environments, with the same password verifiers, session lifetimes,
rules, rate limits, clock and data plane. No password hashing or grant bypass.

`startServe(dir, options)` additionally returns `operatorToken(service =
"operator", days = 1)` and `seedAccounts(options)`. Minting uses the existing
local CLI proof protocol, captures secret stdout in memory and never writes
tokens into proof logs. It confers only that service seat's existing authority.
Tokens may also be requested on production for first-admin setup.

`seedAccounts({roles, provision, args?})` creates N real password accounts per
role, then calls the declared mutation as service:operator; `args(account)`
maps the account to application arguments (default `{principal, role}`).
`provision` is a generated mutation handle or `{name}`, including qualified names such as `accounts.provision`. The returned records
contain email, password, principal, token and expiresAt, grouped by role.
`startServe(dir, {seedUsers: options})` performs the same setup before returning
and exposes those records as `sessions`. Before minting or creating accounts,
the helper requires environment=staging and development=false. Production,
legacy and dev hosts refuse. Inputs are validated before effects; signup is
sequential, bounded, respects identity throttling, and never retries an ambiguous
write. A fresh call creates a fresh random email/password set. Partial failure
does not claim rollback: some accounts/grants may exist; discard the disposable
staging deployment or inspect it before retrying. Application data is created
through ordinary authenticated mutations after provisioning.

Credential records are returned to the operator, never logged by the helper.
The tested guide writes them to an exclusively created 0600 file. They must
not enter source control or reports. There is no public provisioning HTTP
endpoint beyond the application's declared rule-checked mutation.

## 3. First admin

The tested guide uses password signup (which grants no role), then the
filesystem owner's `operatorToken()` to invoke an operator-only mutation.
The roster's insert rule independently requires service:operator. No "first
caller wins", empty-roster bypass, client-selected signup role, or permanent
operator credential in the frontend. The same recipe works on production
with explicit operator-selected email/password; bulk seedAccounts refuses there.
Privileged account tokens cannot mint service tokens. SEC owns lints for
self-bootstrapped global authority; the guide points to this ownership.

## 4. Development doors

For password-only schemas (`auth.password && !auth.guests`), dev disables
`/seed`, every `/dev/*` door (except the existing cryptographically protected
local token protocol), and persona headers by default. The pre-existing serve
GET /dev/latency inspection remains service-authenticated; it never admits an
unauthenticated caller and its reset remains refused. `dev
--unsafe-dev-doors` is explicit opt-in with a prominent warning; serve accepts
no such flag. Host/Origin loopback fences still apply. Door availability is
computed from the current adopted schema, so hot adoption to password-only
also closes them. Seed/reset, clock advance and dev job enqueue revalidate
against the engine schema under the writer immediately before privileged effects;
slow request bodies and requests queued behind adoption cannot retain authority.
Action admission/replay, session-route admission, persona cancellation and upload
owner state transitions likewise revalidate under their actual writer. Previously
admitted durable work retains the existing work-record contract; a refused
new request creates no claimable work.
Persona reads also revalidate against the engine used to evaluate the query,
sync page or asset grant, checking the current declared cast at that read’s
admission. In-flight reads retain their existing snapshot semantics: cast
publication does not lock out concurrent ordinary writes, and the engine
transaction rejects a replaced execution schema.
Change-poll presence entry revalidates under its engine. A detached old
schema is fenced by the engine transaction; a replacement password-only reader
cannot inherit a pre-adoption persona capability. A persona header must name an explicitly declared persona;
an empty declaration admits none. Persona-based schemas retain their ordinary
development workflow. /auth/config always reports development=true on dev,
even with closed doors, so probe tooling can refuse it.

`startDev` follows native persistent storage by default, consuming the old
--no-memory alias; --memory/--fresh explicitly request disposable storage.
The returned now() refuses with guidance if the clock door is closed. Native
readiness plus the per-launch proof marker still establish host identity when
/dev/status is unavailable. Existing fixture/clock tests explicitly opt into
unsafe dev doors when their password schema requires those tools. Generated
frontend proofs explicitly select --memory and --unsafe-dev-doors, preserving
disposable fixture isolation and repeatability under the persistent helper
default. Exact 0.4.30/0.4.31 proof templates are retained and safely adapted
by digest; custom scripts remain untouched. DAY5 owns other starter custody.

## 8. Wave-18 developer loop amendment (DX4)

Implementer: Codex for Charlie Cheever, 2026-10-19, wave-18 fixes #3/#4/#8.
SEC4 owns security campaigns and lint semantics; QRY owns read semantics.
MIG's staging clock is governed by LLP 3000.000.000.002 §4 and unchanged.

`seedAccounts` accepts `service` (default operator, same 1–64 character seat
validation as operatorToken) and merges `args(account)` over `{principal, role}`.
Explicit custom keys override defaults. It validates the seat before effects;
production/dev refusal still precedes mint/signup. Only the chosen service's
existing mutation authority applies. First-admin's tested guide authenticates
first, tries signup only after failed login, and calls the operator-only roster
upsert. Repetition preserves the principal and role; wrong credentials cannot
replace an account or grant. Bulk batches still create fresh random accounts.

Proof `startDev` echoes the closed-door guidance to caller stderr after matching
its per-launch /auth/config marker. Guides start/cheatsheet/personas surface
staging in the ordinary loop. No proof success is inferred from the notice.

Disposable dev already uses a private file/WAL store. It now retains an Owner
and publishes the identical mutual-HMAC/AEAD local token proof as persistent
dev. Locked, private project registry entries include an optional `storePath`.
`token --service` selects a unique live project entry; `--port N` selects among
entries (including closed-door password-only hosts). `--release` is exclusive
with --port. The selected path must still pass existing hardened auxiliary-file,
store-identity, live-owner and mutual-proof checks. Registry data alone grants no
authority; no bearer can mint and no unprotected token door is added. Multiple
hosts refuse implicit selection. Explicit unmatched ports refuse without
falling back to another store. Older records without a proof path request a
restart. Live minting uses the current host clock, matching session resolution
and staging, so time-travel dev does not mint already-expired tokens. Offline
minting retains wall time. Disposable directory ownership and cleanup last for
the whole host lifetime.

Session lifetimes stay seven days on the authoritative application clock.
Every successful or post-advance maintenance-failed clock reply includes a
sessionNotice explaining login after large jumps and upload after time travel;
the clock CLI and staging proof helper echo it on stderr. Reset replies state
that accounts/sessions were removed and cached credentials must be discarded,
then users recreated and roles reprovisioned. This deliberately preserves auth
expiry testing rather than silently extending credentials. Production keeps
its generic auth refusals. Staging's real throttles stay unchanged; the refusal
names Retry-After/retryAfterMs and seedAccounts. Dev loopback already has no
minute counters: scripted dev must serialize KDF work rather than raise a
nonexistent minute limit. This choice avoids a staging/production auth fork.

Upgrade scans bounded authored JS/TS/shell/JSON sources for /seed, /dev/*,
persona headers and startDev calls, skips dependencies/generated/store/output
folders and symlinks, prints per-project paths and migration actions even for
quiet/JSON callers, and returns warnings in JSON. A bounded/incomplete scan
says so. It reports candidates, not a claim that every listed startDev call
lacks --memory. Password-only doors closed and helper persistence began at
0.4.33; scanning also covers surviving risky scripts upgrading from 0.4.33.
Store-lock errors retain recorded PID/address and recommend disposable memory
proofs or stopping the recorded owner. Port conflict probes consult public
/auth/config when closed dev /dev/status refuses; they do not infer non-dev
from a 403.

Evidence: affected unit/native/client tests, packed guide recipes and DX4
cases in Linux consumer qualification; copied 5×wave18 and 5×wave17 upgrade
warning transcripts, assigned Mac Studio affected tests, full crate suites,
ref/docs budget and repository inventory/guide checks. Actual results and any
limits are in WORKSTREAM-REPORT.md; no publication claim or version bump.

DX4 review: [Muse READY](./reviews/dx4/r2-muse.txt) and
