## 9. Wave-19 identity retry and local production lifecycle

Commission: Charlie's day-two addendum, wave-19 fixes #6/#7 (2026-10-19).
This amends the SDK/proof and local release contracts; it grants no new auth
or filesystem authority. SEC4 and QRY keep their existing scopes.

Identity `guest`, `signup` and `login` share a portable request helper with
proof `seedAccounts` (including `startServe({seedUsers})`). Only a delivered
HTTP 429 containing a validated auth `E_RATE_LIMIT` refusal, not marked
`retryable:false`, may retry. The server refuses these requests before account
creation/authentication. Wait for nonnegative integer `retryAfterMs`, or a
valid Retry-After header on older servers (otherwise one second). Preserve the
same credentials and scope, without sending retry options on the wire. Up to
four attempts fit inside the whole request deadline (`timeoutMs`, default
180000); an AbortSignal cancels fetch and waiting. A wait that cannot fit
returns the original refusal with its delay; setup instead throws
E_STAGING_TIMEOUT, warning that partial accounts/grants may remain. Setup
passes its remaining overall budget (default five minutes). There is no
polling at a fixed short interval. Transport errors, malformed responses,
other status/family/codes, permanent refusals, session rotations and role
provisioning mutations never automatically replay. Account/role admission,
peer/email/KDF limits and the staging-before-mint boundary stay unchanged.
These deadlines rely on the fetch implementation honoring AbortSignal, as the
standard fetch does. Custom fetch adapters must honor that contract too.

Deploy and rollback may wait up to five seconds to acquire the actual owner
flock before admission. Missing/unreachable address hints select bounded
waiting; a responsive listener selects the existing authenticated control
status path. If that read-only status fails while shutdown is underway, use
only the remaining acquisition budget, then reread status under the acquired
owner. Neither status nor an address/PID hint admits activation. A subsequent
activation request or ambiguous reply is never replayed automatically. The
exclusive flock, canonical inode/hardlink checks, private auxiliary files,
revision CAS and immutable-source validation remain authoritative. Prune and
other offline command semantics are unchanged. A surviving owner still
refuses E_STORE_BUSY; no process is signalled based on a hint.

`serve DIR --wait-stopped` exposes a five-second lock-release barrier for
callers retaining their own process handle. It requires an existing database,
opens only its existing hardened private owner sidecar, obtains an exclusive
flock and validates the named sidecar/database inode. It does not open SQLite,
create a deployment/sidecar, clear address metadata or signal a PID. No owner
sidecar means no named ownership exclusion. The documented sidecar removal
boundary of LLP 3000.019 §3.4 remains; this is a point-in-time barrier, not a
reservation against a future owner. Other serve flags refuse before effects.

Proof `startServe().stop()` first terminates/reaps the retained native child
through the existing bounded TERM/KILL path, then awaits this barrier, including
any watchdog-held descriptor during worker cleanup. Concurrent/repeated stops
share the in-flight/successful operation. Failure rejects, clears the cached
failure and allows a later barrier retry; it cannot falsely claim cleanup.
No new PID lookup or automatic stop of another owner is introduced. The proof
host stop allowance includes the native child and five-second store barrier.

`data TABLE --json` returns `{rows, more, limit}` for empty and nonempty
snapshots, replacing the bare array. `more` reports the existing one-extra-row
probe in the same read transaction, including default 50-row truncation and
`--limit 0`. Text JSON-lines and the stderr notice are preserved. This operator
surface still bypasses application read rules and refuses private/ephemeral
storage as before; no query semantics change. Existing repository consumers
and the 0.4.35 guide changes are updated for the envelope.

Required evidence: SDK/seed refusal timing, bounded attempts, cancellation and
non-replay tests; actual owner wait/no-effect probes; real delayed worker stop;
deploy/rollback cleanup with a still-listening stale control hint; JSON default
and explicit limit boundaries. Fresh packed Linux qualification must include
real server throttles and public SDK/seedUsers retry, production shutdown and
stdout-only inspection; affected Mac Studio lifecycle tests cover platform
sensitivity. Final exact results, review provenance and scoped limitations are
recorded in WORKSTREAM-REPORT.md.

## 10. Wave-20 loop repairs (DX5)

Commission: Charlie Cheever's wave-20 fix list #4, #6, #7, #8;
implementer Codex, 2026-10-21. This amendment is proposed until its two
independent reviews and implementation evidence are recorded. SEC5 owns
security intent, campaigns and exposure output; this lane changes lookup
advice, never the authority granted by an application rule.

### Clock reports

Amend LLP 3000.000.000.002 §4's proof helper return: `advance(duration)`
returns `{now, fired, held}`. Each entry carries the schedule name, target,
reason, boundary/window metadata and bounded run summary from the existing
operator-only schedule report. `now()` still returns a number. The CLI and
HTTP advance reply expose the same arrays, retaining `schedules` for existing
operator consumers. Fired means a schedule was enqueued, not that its job
succeeded; the run summary distinguishes parked or pending work. Every
non-fired schedule appears in held with a reason, including an already
processed boundary, a future saved boundary, initialization, a future window
or an explicit hold. Saved boundaries survive restart: one fire per boundary,
coalescing missed periods unless eachBoundary was explicitly requested.
The helper and CLI print saved-boundary holds and their recovery action on
stderr, including the equal-boundary case on a reused store. Advance never
rewinds markers or replays a completed boundary. Reply limits account for the
retained report plus its partition into fired/held. Staging's expiry notice
describes expiry/upload recovery without development-door instructions.
Ambiguous or failed advances are never retried; time may already have moved.
Maintenance failures return an explicitly incomplete schedule report with the
advanced time; the proof helper attaches this reply to its thrown error.

### Source diagnostics without an existence oracle

Extend LLP 3000.036.002 §15.2's N_LOOKUP_FILTERED advice to required reads
and reads of written tables. A later write and an asserted `! else CODE` do
not prove read authority. Existing key/flow proofs still suppress advice,
including prior successful exact reads and deliberately public projections.
One note names the source lookup, authored hiding rule, declaration and the
null/custom-refusal consequence; duplicate N_LOOKUP_HIDDEN notes at that
site are avoided (the more specific N_LOOKUP_HIDDEN takes precedence). This is missing-proof advice, not a claim every caller
is refused. Program `exists` and rule-witness `exists` keep distinct semantics.

For private tables with secondary unique keys, source advice explains that
an unreadable conflicting row uses generic E_RULE (or an undisclosed write
target miss), even when the unique declaration has `else CODE`. The named
constraint applies only when the conflict can be disclosed. Do not return
the declared code only on hidden conflicts: that would violate LLP 3000 §7
and LLP 3000.036.002 §15.2. Public E_RULE repair text, if changed, is identical
for ordinary rule rejection and hidden collision. No row, key, actual hiding
clause or hidden-dependent meter enters the public refusal. Rewrites propose
a minimal readable key projection or operator-mediated ownership/claim flow,
never broader disclosure of private rows. Paired hidden/missing lookup tests assert equality of public diagnostics and
logical meters. Hidden/ordinary write-refusal tests compare public refusals
and receipts; write replies expose no meter.

### Upgrade advice reaches the old CLI

Extend §8's bounded scan with candidate `data ... --json` consumers in authored
scripts, including argv-array and shell forms. List paths without printing
source. State the one-line migration `JSON.parse(stdout).rows` for the former
bare array, and preserve `more`/`limit`. This is a candidate scan, not an AST
proof or an automatic rewrite; report scan limits.

The installed wrapper runs project warnings before the first ordinary check
for that installed version, independently of the runtime-history receipt.
A warning receipt is written only after delivery to a terminal (or an empty
scan). Piped/captured stderr cannot establish delivery: old quiet upgrades
discard it, so a nonempty scan stays unacknowledged and the next ordinary
check repeats the advice, including in CI. Baseline checks neither deliver
nor acknowledge warnings; read/receipt failures do not fail compilation.
Warnings always use stderr, preserving one-object JSON stdout and quiet-mode
visibility. This reaches the usual published 0.4.33/0.4.35 upgrade path because
their upgrade invokes the newly installed wrapper for check. A fresh-process
resolution must select new bytes after package replacement. Direct upgrade
keeps its existing pre-install warning behavior. Test both published old CLIs
against the fresh packed package in an isolated local registry, including
--quiet and --json --quiet and the deferred first check; do not claim
an upgrade was tested by invoking only the new helper.

### Frontend and starter custody

Extend LLP 3000.013.002 §2 with `ReadState` in snapback4/react: a list read
(or PageHook) renders loading, denied, empty, or authorized data through one
component. It adds no subscription, cache or authority. It preserves partial
and stale rows; empty means the returned list is empty, never proven absence.
Loading and empty default to null; denied uses the supplied renderer or
throws the existing QueryRefusal for an error boundary. Children receive the
typed list and precise settled read metadata. Browser and React Native
callers supply their own display elements.

The Expo adapter owns `snapback4-expo/metro` (CommonJS withSnapback(config))
and its wasm transformer. Resolve Expo's transformer relative to the consuming
project/config, compatible with isolated package-manager installs. Preserve
the caller's config and append the existing .snapback4 block and wasm support.
New starter Metro config only obtains Expo's default and calls withSnapback.
The adapter also owns the native smoke sign-in hook; new starters import it
instead of carrying src/native-smoke.ts. Password and guest selection remain
explicit; ordinary launches never sign in automatically. Adapt removes a recognized old helper only when the planned source no longer
references it; custom references, modified helpers and unknown source symlinks
retain application custody. Old generated Metro prose remains recognizable
when adapting an untouched README. No native engine or simulator custody changes.

Amend LLP 3000.011.003.000 §7.2: adapt replaces an untouched todo frontend
proof with a runnable proof scaffold retaining frontend:proof/proof:web and
Playwright. It starts the correct frontend and checks rendered content, then
explicitly refuses to claim an app-specific write proof until the builder
adds one. A public schema without identity or personas skips sign-in and still
checks rendering before the missing-scenario refusal. A custom proof is never
rewritten. Fresh non-todo starters get the
same scaffold. Every Expo starter includes playwright-core, including custom
schemas. Qualification runs changed guide/starter sources from the packed
tarball, tests the expected scaffold refusal, and records frontend character
reductions on copies of three wave-20 Expo lanes. No original lane is edited.

### Acceptance and scope

Full five-crate Rust tests, affected client tests, fresh-pack Linux consumer
qualification with per-item cases and published-old-CLI upgrades, Mac Studio
affected platform tests, ref-check, docs budget and repository-root checks.
No test.sh, publication, push or version bump is authorized by this work.
WORKSTREAM-REPORT.md records exact commands/results, commits and limitations;
review transcripts and source provenance live in llp/reviews/dx5/.


## 11. Wave-22 loop repairs (DX6)

Commission: Charlie Cheever's wave-22 fixes #5, #6 and #8 (2026-10-22).
Implementer: Codex in sb4-b22-dx6. This amends §10, the staging clock of
LLP 3000.000.000.002 §4, supplied sessions in LLP 3000.036.004 §15.4,
and the starter application of LLP 3000.013.002 §2. SEC7 owns security advice,
intent, campaigns, upload recipes and the password/roles recipe.
This proposal is subject to the requested fresh Muse and Codex reviews.

### Session input and compatibility

Seeded records preserve the actual signup session's kind alongside its
principal, token and numeric expiresAt. They can be passed directly as Session.
Online createClient accepts a legacy incomplete session literal as token-only
transport credentials: its token must be nonempty; partial principal, kind and
expiry metadata never establishes identity, refresh timing or authority. The
server resolves the bearer; session() is null and there is no refresh timer,
as for the existing token option. Complete shapes remain strictly validated
and privately snapshotted. Local/device session input remains complete-only.
E_SESSION lists every missing/invalid field without values and gives the exact
one-line online repair createClient({ url, token }). An ISO expiry in a complete
shape refuses instead of creating a NaN timer. Restored full sessions retain
the existing restore validation and server expiry semantics.

### Advances, maintenance and retained boundaries

ClockAdvance remains an object reporting now/fired/held; valueOf returns now
for arithmetic, ordering and new Date(result). This is JavaScript numeric
coercion, not strict-equality compatibility; typed callers use result.now.

For classified staging, advance(duration) preserves remaining ordinary session
lifetimes by default. The core advances valid full/read session created/expiry
fields, read caps and recoverable mint receipts by the same checked delta,
in the same transaction as existing worker-lease preservation, before publishing
the new process clock. Expired, capped, revoked or superseded authority cannot
become live. Selection uses the authority kernel and bounded pages; overflow
refuses atomically. Existing action delegated sessions and supervised service
families remain owned by the worker-lease path, without double shifting.
Historical admission timestamps are evidence, not an ongoing cap; application
deadlines/backoffs remain business time.

Preservation includes SDK custody, not just raw HTTP credentials. A staging
response for the exact request bearer can publish authoritative session expiry
and read cap beside the same locked business-time/revision snapshot, obtained
through a detached store-identity/liveness-checked authority read. No bearer,
new authority, mint, rotation or refresh is exposed. Production publishes no
such metadata. A failed detached timing read suppresses the clock sample,
including streaming-final samples, instead of publishing advanced business
time with stale credential metadata. A client reconciles only its current
bearer's matching request URL/header and monotonically increases its live
expiry/cap before clock listeners run. Local/device clients await durable
credential custody before publishing or persisting their business clock.
Online clients keep a volatile clock; their existing session listeners may
persist custody asynchronously. Authenticated restoration still validates
expired metadata with the staging probe; no online durability barrier is implied.
Heartbeat final frames carry the same matching-bearer timing or unavailable
evidence as ordinary response headers. Reconciliation and the corresponding
local/device clock publication are serialized: durable credential saves are awaited
before publishing or persisting the advanced clock. A failed save leaves the
clock unchanged, retains dirty credential timing for retry, and surfaces as a
transport failure; rotation/close fences also suppress stale clock publication.
App preparation retains its existing private credential staging: prepared local
clock offsets remain non-durable, including on discard/close, until the actual
App credential commit succeeds. Only then may clock persistence activate before
the scope is published. A later clock-save failure reports a signed-in warning
and retries through ordinary device work; it cannot roll back durable identity.
The existing per-invocation response cutoff (LLP 3000.013 §6 and §12.7) also
spans implicit scope retirement's local credential cleanup. A scope-owned
reference count retains capture before teardown and through each scheduled
local credential task, releasing on rollback or close without waiting for an
auth operation or remote revocation queue.
Capture occurs synchronously when the response decoder validates a body,
before caller Promise continuations can cross that cutoff.
An invocation retains a body validated while live through settlement; a
completed capture owner cannot reopen its cutoff through another begin or hold.
Retention preserves a decoded body, not a stale authentication classification.
An E_AUTH refusal remains scoped to the bearer revision actually dispatched:
rotation supersedes prior and intermediate retiring-bearer revisions, including
when the response was decoded before rotation or arrives after cancellation or
a retryable refresh failure. Recheck that authority when consuming retained
responses. A successor already dispatched during credential persistence remains
current; its own refusal may sign it out. Sign-out alone does not supersede a
same-bearer refusal, and sent outcomes and business refusals retain their ordinary
invocation custody. Retryable refresh failure still permits a same-id retry under
the current credential revision.
Rotated/logged-out credentials cannot be restored by a late response. Client
clocks are isolated, so one bearer's response cannot expire another before its
own timing is reconciled. Read startup verifies before scheduling expiry;
an expired restored metadata image requires a successful authenticated read-only
staging probe with matching viewer/scope and live timing. Production/offline
without this evidence keeps the existing expiry refusal. The local constructor
reconciles bootstrap timing before applying a restored device clock's expiry
check. Tests retain actual read clients and restore them across their old
absolute expiry, compare two independent bearers, and exercise explicit-expiry
and production controls. These headers are staging timing evidence only;
ordinary authority is still checked on every server admission. Real elapsed time still consumes
credentials. sessions:'expire' explicitly tests expiry with the existing
business clock. Dev retains its existing expiry behavior. Production rejects
all clock controls and never calls preservation. Restart keeps the persisted
credential timestamps and drops only the existing process-local business offset.
This intentional staging-only simulated jump also shifts a read family's cap;
ordinary production read-cap immutability is unchanged.

advance(duration, {drain:false}) advances time and pauses background maintenance
before releasing the writer. This covers expiry sweeps, scheduled enqueue,
queued job chunks, asset collection, view recount and delivery maintenance,
so a mutation can exercise its own deadline check. Authorization and logical
row expiry still apply to ordinary queries/mutations. The pause lasts until
host.drain(), another draining advance, or process restart. drain() uses the
same authenticated endpoint with duration:'0ms', drain:true, advancing no time
and resuming normal coalesced maintenance. eachBoundary requires drain:true.
The HTTP report includes maintenancePaused; native CLI spells these controls
clock advance D --no-drain and clock drain. Failed/ambiguous requests are never
automatically replayed. A failed drain leaves its advanced time intact, its
report explicitly incomplete, and maintenance paused. Only a successful explicit
drain resumes it. drain() advances no time and safely continues existing queued
work/checkpoints; never repeat a lost advance to obtain that recovery.

A saved boundary is future-held only when it is strictly greater than the
boundary of the requested effective schedule window. Equality means that the
current window was already processed: report not-due, without consulting wall
time. Repeated advances inside that window and zero-time drains succeed without
allowHeld, including recovery of queued work after a failed drain completion.
Never enqueue the processed window again.
A draining advance whose saved future boundary blocks requested work refuses
E_CLOCK_HELD before clock, session or lease effects. The refusal names the
schedule, saved boundary, next unprocessed window and recovery duration to
reach the saved boundary from the unchanged process clock, not from the rejected
requested time. Relative recovery hints in accepted reports likewise use the
actual process clock, including when a disclosure floor is ahead of it.
A held report sets heldUntil to that saved boundary and
nextBoundary to the next unprocessed boundary. Catching up to heldUntil
reports not-due and never re-enqueues the processed window; reaching nextBoundary
fires once. Fresh staging storage and continuing with the original offset are
recovery choices; saved markers never rewind. allowHeld:true (CLI --allow-held) explicitly accepts a
retained boundary. Intentional drain:false pauses and dev --hold-schedules are
explicit holds. not-due/initialization remains a successful reported outcome.
Control authorization/classification is checked again under the actual writer.

### Upgrade advice and future formats

Advice is scoped to actual version transitions and each behavior's introduction
version. A fresh init/check is silent. Delivered stderr is acknowledged durably
for non-TTY callers too; baseline checks neither emit nor acknowledge advice.
The new upgrade helper retains warning stderr even under --quiet. Published
older quiet CLIs discard their check child's stderr without signalling this;
that historical capture cannot be distinguished from normal non-TTY delivery.
Advice from that old quiet path may therefore be acknowledged without display;
guide changes remains available. No ancestor
process inspection or script mutation is introduced.

The bounded candidate scan covers partial session literals and numeric advance
uses, explicit persistent startDev calls and data --json consumers. Explicit
nearby refusal assertions do not become dev-door warnings. Candidate paths,
never source or credentials, are printed; incomplete scans remain disclosed.
Future known-family store formats refuse with 'a newer Snapback (FORMAT)'.
Read-only SQL inspection validates the format before exposing rows and exits
nonzero on refusal. Already published old binaries cannot be repaired.

### Starter and proof rendering

Both list starters render through the packaged ReadState. Proven absence and
partial empty results retain distinct text, with existing freshness and
pagination semantics unchanged. Rename the docs' local ReadState example to
ReadNotice so it does not shadow the export. Password clients omit persona
selection and explicit web witness/generated API imports. The proof driver installs the
existing witness bridge before app creation; createApp calls an immutable Symbol observer only under explicit witness=web.
This is a public same-origin test channel, not a secret or an authentication
boundary. A witness URL alone installs no observer and exposes no App global.
The driver installs its nonconfigurable/nonwritable observer before application
scripts and locks/freezes the selected witness bridge; the first App remains
selected for that page. Same-App explicit API registration can enrich it;
a different explicit App refuses E_WITNESS_APP_SELECTION and requires a separate
page. Later automatic Apps cannot silently redirect the proof. Application JS
remains trusted to implement the application: same-origin code can forge its
own test observer outside a driven page, just as it can read web session storage.
The observer grants no new credentials or backend authority. Ordinary bundles
carry only the creation dispatch, not the witness implementation. No-API
registration captures only durable non-ephemeral mutation handles; direct
witness mutate still requires generated API.

Proof text locators match normalized entire descendant text, including composed
React Native spans and wrapping labels. Choose smallest matching visible,
non-editable elements; independent matches retain strict Playwright ambiguity.
Whitespace normalization collapses runs and trims both ends; case is preserved,
with no Unicode normalization or input value matching. Exact strings are case-sensitive;
explicit substring strings are case-insensitive and regex follows its pattern/flags.
String matching stays exact by default; substring is explicit, never a silent
fallback. A composed label cannot make an unrelated sibling count as success.
Text ranges outside overflow clips do not contribute evidence to a visible
ancestor. Layoutless wrappers may forward their visible descendants; a clipped
suffix cannot manufacture a complete status label.

Run complete crate tests, affected client and assigned Mac Studio tests,

# LLP 3000.036.004: Security invariants and exposure

**Type:** RFC
**Status:** Accepted (SEC design revisions 3/5 and SEC2 amendment/implementation round 5: Muse and fresh Codex READY; qualification in progress)
**Systems:** Snapback 4 Quarry authorization, check, audit, generated security tests, validation
**Author:** Codex for Charlie Cheever (SEC)
**Date:** 2026-10-18
**Revised:** 2026-10-21 (SEC5 §14 and SEC6 §15; both independently reviewed; SEC6 scoped qualification complete; code snapshot4578e98bed)
**Related:** [LLP 3000.036](./3000.036-what-the-app-farm-asks-of-the-rule-language.rfc.md), [LLP 3000.035](./3000.035-quarry-semantics-in-lean.plan.md), [LLP 3000.014](./3000.014-a-child-reads-through-its-parent.rfc.md), [LLP 3000.038](./3000.038-file-assets.rfc.md)

## 1. Contract

The wave-16 bakeoff found rules enforced correctly but policies encoded wrongly.
A declaration of intent is independent of the rules implementing it. `check`
reports each declaration as **proved**, **refuted**, or **unproved**. Refuted
means a concrete, replayed database/rule counterexample, never merely a Boolean
assignment. Unproved names the unsupported path or incomplete search. Neither
unproved nor a finite passing test campaign may be described as proved.

Implementer: SEC in this worktree, starting 2026-10-18. The author commissioned
this semantic extension and two independent design reviews. No version bump
or publication is part of this lane. STAGE owns provisioning/password dev doors;
RULES5 owns live-parent rule semantics; FRONT owns general diagnostic triage.

## 2. Surface

Use the existing rule vocabulary rather than invent a second policy language:

```
invariant notes.read only .patient = viewer or .clinician = viewer
invariant requests.update only .requester != viewer
invariant members.role write only exists roles[viewer, role = 'owner']
invariant photos always .image != null
```

The first target is a table, the second component an effect (`read`, `insert`,
`update`, `delete`) or a column followed by `write`. `write` checks insert and
update, including both images for ordinary updates; delete authority has its
own declaration. A column invariant only concerns writes to that column, but
must include every effective admission path. Owner-only field patches bypass
an ordinary table update rule; invariants affected by `written by` stay
unproved until that bypass is modeled. An implication from a denied table
rule must never prove such an owned-field claim.
`always` is a row-integrity assertion. Predicates parse as ordinary Quarry
expressions; unsupported policy expressions are reported unproved with the
reason. Unknown tables/columns/effects are authoring errors. Multiple source
files and multiple declarations are supported. For update intent `.field` means both old and next images for mutable
columns; named transitions require an explicit reviewed reduction or stay
unproved. Once-judged immutable/id rules need a proved equal-image reduction
or stay unproved. Both upsert arms and `insert if absent` are included, with
their own collision/refusal observations. `always` quantifies over every
committed row image from insert/update/upsert and trusted seed/import/restore/
activation, not merely mutation inserts. Constraint-based row proof must use
the actual validation on every ingress, including defaults and the exact
non-whitespace minimum function, or stay unproved.

No declaration changes runtime
authority or replaces a rule. No implicit service-seat exemption is added.

The proof fragment uses bound rule predicates. A row assertion can be proved
from its required column type/constraints (not an optional type), or otherwise
remains unproved. Aggregate/transition/temporal assertions outside that fragment
remain explicitly unproved, not syntactically discarded. Syntax with `now`,
counts, or other program expressions must retain that reason. This is a safe
extension point, not a claim of a complete solver for arbitrary Quarry.

## 3. Sound proof boundary

For a table effect, prove `admission => policy` for **every database snapshot**,
row image, ordinary authenticated viewer (including service seats) and clock.
The engine system principal is explicitly outside this quantification: it is
the trusted seed/import/job boundary, never an ordinary user or an implicit
service-seat exemption. Tables touched by system/native/job/worker paths remain
unproved absent a reviewed reduction, and audit lists those writers. This overapproximates every reachable history:
an old assignment and a changed current role are independent facts. Grant
creation never proves a current role. Required role predicates must be true at
the access boundary. No fixture-specific assumption enters a proof.

Translate Boolean connectives compositionally, retaining true/false/unknown
truth for atomic predicates. Unknown never admits and `not unknown` is unknown.
Atomic facts are keyed by their full bound structure, including table, index,
keys, named equalities and old/next image. Symmetric equality may canonicalize by operand reordering only, preserving
Value variants (Id is not Text), table, index, keys, image and predicate kind;
other equalities and probes stay independent. A finite exhaustive implication
check over this abstraction is sound because it includes every concrete
valuation, even impossible ones. Cap atoms/work; cap exhaustion is unproved.
Do not add database consistency axioms without a separate soundness argument.
Never drop, assume true/false, or simplify an unsupported admission atom;
keep it opaque with its full identity or report unproved. Concrete leaf
semantics are the current `evaluate_leaf`/`term`, not stale Lean open points:
null equals null, null differs from a non-null literal, Id differs from Text,
noninteger ordered comparison returns false, and a missing live reference
marks unknown (including under negation). Missing ordinary fields currently
load null; missing reference and missing image are not conflated. Any semantic
mismatch with the independent model is named, never normalized away. Runtime
errors do not establish an admitted result; probe/storage/schema failure
cannot be used as a successful counterexample or a proof fact.

The Lean addition proves a three-valued Kleene kernel with admission only
on Readable and the exact theorem: exhaustive checking implies that for every
valuation, eval(admission) = Readable implies eval(policy) = Readable; the Quarry-to-kernel translation and runtime boundary remain reviewed
Rust obligations, not a claim of whole-platform formal verification.

For read intent, admission includes the ordinary read rule and every bypass:
- point/list/view/filter/count/exists and live refetch use ruled reads;
- sync acquisition and publication authorize at their own server snapshot. An
  offline device cannot know a later server revocation, even with until-revoked.
  A synced read invariant therefore reports the device access path unproved
  for current-server-role intent, separately from its server proof. Delivered
  history has an additional explicit retained-history blocker. No stale local
  role is treated as a current server role;
- inherited read-through rules are checked in their bound form, including
  captures; live-parent semantics remain RULES5's responsibility;
- valued write targets already reread through `get` before returning, and
  generated insert results also use an ordinary ruled read. Verify those
  reductions against the bound IR; any escaping image without that reduction
  is a blocker or must satisfy the implication `effective write admission => read intent` for that image;
  otherwise the declaration stays unproved;
- maintained aggregates/columns and row views may expose source changes under
  different rules: report such source claims unproved unless a reviewed exact
  reduction proves them; projections narrow payload only; existence/count disclosure follows the
  derived path's own rules, so each derived path needs its own reduction or
  stays unproved;
- table-rule probes see raw target rows, unlike program `exists`. Follow
  reverse dependencies into every other table's read/write rules: the presence
  of a marker row or a successful write can disclose the protected target's
  existence or named fields without returning that target. Source privacy
  intent remains unproved for such raw-probe observations unless a reviewed
  reduction proves authorization or the policy explicitly permits disclosure;
- incoming `on delete cascade` and `on delete set null` effects bypass child
  delete/update rules. Report child delete/update/column-write invariants
  unproved when affected, including transitive cascades, until initiating
  authority and child-image policy are modeled. Enumerate these edges in audit;
- asset reads inherit their owning row privacy, while upload/write authority
  belongs to insert/update intent; applicable private-field authorities must be conjoined with owning-row
  admission for asset reads;
- jobs, schedules, native jobs, actions and external effects are trusted system
  or worker boundaries. Read claims affected by opaque outputs/side effects
  remain unproved. Job writes do not prove ordinary-user write authority;
- refusal codes are observations: an authored difference between an absent
  lookup and later denial is a reported exposure. A privacy proof must not
  ignore that path. Unmodeled constraint/refusal observations remain unproved.

Observer boundary: this verifies row payload and logical existence/refusal
observations, not physical timing, runtime cost or all resource side channels.
The platform's documented examined-count/meter-cut observations are explicitly
excluded and reported as exclusions, not full noninterference. Read intent
includes all logical exposures above. A component may be proved while the
whole declaration remains unproved because another path is blocked.

The implementation must build a closed-world census of bound IR read/write
forms and schema-triggered paths. An unclassified form is a blocker, never
silently omitted. Census includes sequence allocation/read admission, online
and device query paths, ephemeral paths, owner fields, maintained writes and
referential actions. System/job/action/native/external touched tables default
unproved without a reviewed reduction, and are listed as grant-column writers.
Every `read` declaration covers all enumerated logical paths, not just its
direct rule. Authenticated viewer classes use engine operations; signed-out
cases run only against HTTP/auth admission, never a fabricated principal.
Retained-history observations are classified by leave policy and reported
separately; they cannot refute the platform's retention contract or prove a
current-role declaration. Test output names unsupported device freshness.

The report enumerates the paths checked and blockers. A proof is never awarded
just because the direct table rule passed while an indirect path is unmodeled.
Conservative rejection/notes are acceptable; false proof is not.

## 4. Counterexamples and generated tests

Generate deterministic challenges from schema types, policy atoms and fixture
rows. Use in-memory stores; never leave SQLite sidecars under target. Vary the
viewer across owner/other-user/other-role/revoked-role/unauthenticated classes,
policy literals, principal arguments and absent optional values. Existing role
rows and retained grant rows form revoked-role snapshots. Do not call an
arbitrary consistent snapshot a *reachable* application-operation sequence.

Concrete counterexamples must replay the engine's actual rule admission and
show the policy false, recording viewer, effect, row, supporting rows and rule
path. The absence of a concrete witness when implication fails is **unproved**.
Generated tests are a separate executable check, run by default `test`, with
coverage counts and named unsupported cases. They use isolated state so they
cannot corrupt the fixture business tests. For operations, derive arguments
from fixtures and schema, substitute other principals and roles, and compare
admitted effects/observations against the declared intent. Merely succeeding
as another user is not a failure when policy permits that operation. Signed-out
network admission cannot be tested by inventing a signed-in principal: label
that boundary separately. No finite campaign promises arbitrary sequence
coverage. `test` fails on replayed violations; unproved coverage is explicit.

## 5. Exposure report

`audit` and `check --audit`, both with `--json`, produce a stable structured
report. This is a conservative permission map, not a claim every listed path
is reachable. Enumerate each table/effect, row predicate, audience-readable
and owner-private columns, operations touching it, sync/asset/derived paths,
and inherited dependencies. List probes and the insert/update writers of the
probed grant columns; include transitive dependencies with a visited set.
Enumerate role alternatives found in rule probes/literals, including generic
signed-in principals and service seats. Unmodeled role predicates retain their
full expression rather than collapsing to an invented role name. Normal
`check` lists broad signed-in reads and tables with no declared intent, with
`guide security` as the next step. Do not claim `allow` admits signed-out
requests; authentication precedes the operation.

## 6. Bakeoff repairs

Add advisory lints (not unsound policy proofs) for grants lacking current-role
rechecks, argument writes into reader-grant columns, open `created` bootstrap
of globally trusted authority (extend N_VACUOUS_RULE), optional evidence, and
sweep-only status gates. Name the rule/column/operation and the safe recipe.
An existence-oracle advisory compares distinct authored absent/denied codes;
it must acknowledge the read rule may already hide the row. Do not silently
rewrite authored codes, which are a public application contract; privacy intent
must account for the resulting observation or remain unproved.

Text minimums count non-whitespace Unicode scalar values (`char::is_whitespace`);
maximums continue to count all scalar values. This applies to arguments, rows,
optional/list-contained text on server/device, without changing stored bytes.
Document the behavioral change and test ASCII/Unicode whitespace and mixed
text. Media stays optional only when the product allows omission; required
photos use required `image` or `[image] 1..N`, with existing content validation.

## 7. Qualification and limits

Add adversarial compiler/engine tests for proof soundness, unknown predicates,
atom limits, indirect blockers, role revocation, grants and named transitions.
Extend the independent Lean model for the propositional kernel. Include
regressions for owned-field bypass with deny update, cascade and set-null
against denied child rules, raw-rule existence observations, and disconnected
server/replica role revocation. Pin original
and repaired wave-16 reproductions with their intended policy; retain exact
source provenance, and explain ambiguous specs (045) and missing transitions
(015), never manufacture evidence for an operation the source lacks.
Run all 50 wave-16 and 100 wave-15 schemas, reporting pre-existing diagnostics,
new warnings and unproved assertions separately. Unannotated applications have
no new false proof/refusal claims; they receive discoverability notes. Include
actual default generated-test execution, not only parsing or lint counts.

Guide cards, README and starters lead to `guide security`; runnable new Quarry
examples must also compile using a freshly packed CLI. Add 0.4.32 guide changes.
Run affected tests, full requested crate/client/differential qualifications,
wasm measurement and budget (measurement + 500 B with reason), ref/docs/root
checks. Record exact commands, results and any genuine environment limits in
WORKSTREAM-REPORT.md. Do not count an incomplete qualification as green.

## 8. Operation and general row assertions (SEC refinement)

The table effect contract is intentionally stronger than a query/mutation
contract. To state an operation-specific authority rule without overrestricting
other writers, `invariant vehicles.liftHold only exists roster[viewer, role =
'liaison']` targets the unique authored mutation `liftHold` on vehicles.
Qualified operation names are allowed; ambiguous/unknown names are errors.
Only writes to the named table by that operation are covered. Its earlier
straight-line requirements may establish admission when they bind to existing
rule predicates: positive caller-filtered existence implies raw existence,
whereas negative existence is not assumed equivalent. Branch/loop guards,
aliases, helper calls, changed viewer, prior writes, and unsupported flow remain
unproved unless separately reduced. The current conservative implementation
uses only leading straight-line requirements before any other statement, and
only requirements without negative probes or live references. These require
facts are evaluated before writes; a policy depending on a table any earlier
statement can change cannot be proved. Require-to-write stability is checked
against every intervening write. Failure to establish it is unproved. The
actual effective write rule remains an additional obligation, including the
field-owner bypass and implicit effects. No operation syntax grants authority.

General `always` expressions can still receive concrete counterexamples even
when outside the proof fragment. Preserve the original policy AST; a separate
partial concrete evaluator can judge row-local values, Boolean connectives,
comparisons, server clock and raw named-key existence over a schema-valid
snapshot. Unsupported/unknown evaluation is not false and cannot refute.
Nonunique raw existence is an explicit existential over all stored live rows,
not a fabricated unique index or a caller-filtered program read. Unmodeled
expiry/captures/derived tables block this evaluator. Snapshot-seeded violations
are labeled as such, never reachable application traces. Actual authored
operation challenges use the engine, check committed changed images and name
the operation and arguments; no-op/rolled-back or merely successful unrelated
operations cannot refute a write policy. Fixtures and generated cross-principal
role rows may supply candidates, but never proof assumptions. Multi-operation
history, HTTP and device traces remain separately named coverage obligations.

### 8.1 Exact conservative boundary (review clarification)

A snapshot-only evaluation NEVER sets refuted. A row-state counterexample must
actually execute Engine::seed_at in an in-memory engine and then read back the
committed image before judging it; defaults, unique/final constraints, typed
validation and the exact text minimum must pass. That is a replay of the trusted
seed ingress in the `always` quantification, labeled `trusted-seed ingress`,
not proof that an ordinary application sequence reaches it. Rejected seeding,
nonlive/expired/retained/captured/derived populations or unsupported validation
are unproved, never refuted. No mutation is inferred from a snapshot.

The concrete evaluator uses the typed Value and exact §3 leaf/connective
semantics; typed Id and Text stay distinct. Its partial unsupported cases
produce unknown/unsupported, never false, including under Boolean connectives.
It supports no clock/temporal expressions in this increment: `now` or temporal
comparisons remain unproved. It does not borrow the host language's truthiness.

Operation proof is confined to one atomic server mutation transaction. The
interpreter/SQLite transaction admits no concurrent application interleaving
between requirements and its writes; opaque/external work is excluded. Leading
requirements contribute only row-independent viewer/literal/positive raw-probe
facts; every probe is caller-filtered at runtime so positivity is essential.
No fact binds an old/next target field, argument alias or captured row. Policy
expressions needing those bindings stay unproved in this reduction. Reject a
require dependency if ANY operation write may touch it, including the target
write itself, both upsert arms, field-authority paths, maintains, sequences and
referential actions. Unknown/helper/opaque write sets or unclassified forms
force unproved; the absence of an explicit IR write is not an absence proof.
These are conservative blockers, not proposed rewrite/lint assumptions.

## 10. SEC2 observer and adoption amendment

Implementer: SEC2, 2026-10-18. This amendment extends, rather than weakens,
the snapshot quantification and the proved/refuted/unproved contract above.
It is a proposal until the independent reviews and implementation evidence
are recorded. STAGE owns HTTP provisioning and password dev doors; RULES5
owns live-parent semantics; FRONT owns general diagnostic triage.

### 10.1 Separate observer obligations

Report individual observer obligations as well as the whole verdict. A proved
component never clears another unresolved component. Ordinary point, scan,
planned union/projection, count, sum and existence reads consume authorized
rows; pure computation over those rows cannot reveal an unauthorized payload.
The reduction concerns logical data, not the already excluded examined-count,
meter, physical timing or the separately unproved global wire activity path.
Context changes, native programs and external workers are never pure reads.

For a maintained count or sum with ordinary bare group keys, pull the derived
read predicate back to the source row by substituting its group columns.
Prove that predicate implies the source invariant using the existing exhaustive
kernel. Do not assume the source read rule protects an explicitly broader
aggregate. Lost source fields, value-dependent derived rules, aliases,
row-keyed/private/captured maintenance, temporal contributions and downstream
derived observers without a checked substitution stay unproved with the exact
edge and an author repair. A filter can narrow contributors, but is not used
as an assumption in this first reduction. No maintenance consistency axiom is
added to the propositional kernel.

Generate paired in-memory engine worlds, identical except for one protected
row, only when both worlds seed and validate and the privacy policy is false
in both. Execute the same authored operation with identical arguments/viewer
and clock. Different returned data or refusal code/message is a concrete
logical-existence counterexample; ignore sequence numbers, receipts, meters
and timing. Keep both executions and inputs in the witness. An engine/storage
error or unsupported policy evaluation cannot refute. A passing finite paired
campaign proves nothing. Maintenance is rebuilt independently in each world;
never seed a fabricated derived value. Unsupported referential/final-existence
worlds are declined. This tests count/sum/existence, mutation returns and
collision/refusal observations without guessing which successful call is bad.

### 10.2 Temporal intent

A separate, typed clock reduction accepts Boolean combinations of ordinary
rule predicates and comparisons between server `now` and row time fields.
It adds the actual half-open lifetime predicate (nullable lower/upper bounds
included) to read admission. Clock atoms use a compiler-private identity and
cannot alias user fields. Only equivalent operand orderings canonicalize;
there is no inferred inequality arithmetic. A read opening/expiry component
can therefore be proved independently of sweep execution. Public payload is
hidden before `not before` and after `expire at`, even while physical rows
await cleanup. A job that flips a flag establishes no exact deadline: temporal
intent without a matching lifetime or dominating clock gate stays unproved
or receives an executed between-ticks counterexample. Derived lifetime paths
are not silently covered by the direct-row reduction. Offline time/revocation
retains the existing applied-server-position boundary.

### 10.3 Adoption

Normal check emits one project-level N_SECURITY_INTENT note counting tables
with any effective access rule and no invariant. Generate a separate candidate
draft in `snapback/generated/security-invariants.q.draft`, with provenance and
an explicit author-confirmation warning. It is never compiled or accepted
automatically. Candidate read/insert/delete predicates repeat existing rules
as a starting point, not inferred product intent; omit unsupported synthetic
or transition forms with an explanation. Stable content is deterministic and
rewritten only when changed. The note is once per check, not suppressed forever
by hidden state: a changed schema must remain discoverable. An invariant on
one effect does not cover another. Audit ends with conditional role/row/effect
exposures lacking a matching invariant; this is syntactic coverage, never proof
coverage. Unproved and refuted declared effects remain visible in verdicts.

Every added guide/starter form is executed against an installed tarball. The
README and start packet introduce invariants together with rules, within the
existing documentation budget. Candidate declarations require the author to
compare against the app specification, particularly current roles, grants,
counts, time and omitted evidence; copying rules alone cannot catch a wrongly
encoded specification.

### 10.4 Reduction details and review clarifications

The exact live predicate is `(lower IS NULL OR lower <= now) AND
(upper IS NULL OR now < upper)`, using materialized column defaults just as
the runtime does. Tests include equality ticks, nulls and defaults. The clock
symbol cannot be serialized as a runtime RuleTerm: its identity contains a
colon, which Quarry column names cannot contain. Reversal maps `a >= b` to
`b <= a` and `a > b` to `b < a`, without changing strictness. Only the pinned
server lifetime clock enters this theorem; a query's rounded read-time value
and a device's host clock do not establish admission. Raw probes and every
derived lifetime observer remain separate obligations/blockers. Schedules do
not constrain the time between deadline and sweep. Any between-ticks witness
must execute actual engine calls at both clocks from independently validated
seed ingress; snapshot evaluation of `now` alone never refutes.

Both paired worlds use §8.1's actual `Engine::seed_at`, committed read-back,
typed/default/unique/final-existence validation, and exact text minima. The
named read invariant is evaluated for the same viewer and hypothetical
protected row, against each world's committed snapshot and identical clock;
unknown is not false. These are seed-ingress worlds, not a reachability proof.
Engine contexts are authenticated only. HTTP signed-out and offline/device
histories remain separately labeled. Compare typed canonical object values
and engine-defined ordered arrays; do not sort away meaningful order. Decline
generated ids/opaque work, incomplete results and any observation that does
not repeat when recreating each world. Random/store-specific cursors are not
counterexamples. Explicitly record the unproved sequence/receipt/wire boundary
and excluded timing/meter boundary even when payloads agree. Only a change in
the protected row is an experimental input; other seed rows remain identical,
and referentially invalid absence worlds are declined.

Pullback preserves typed Value variants, full probe table/index/key/equality
identity and row images. Only bare identically typed group columns substitute;
derived id/value, reference and old/next fields do not. Kernel node/atom cap
exhaustion is unproved. The direct edge can be proved as a component; any
downstream derivation lacking a transitive substitution blocks the whole
declaration. Do not infer transitive privacy from that component result.

The missing-intent note includes public/allow tables and tables with any
non-deny read/insert/update/delete rule; a wholly denied table needs no note.
It is emitted once in each check result without persistent suppression state,
alongside any distinct broad-read advice. Drafts are ignored generated output,
never source or an inventory leaf; stale content is regenerated, never a check
refusal. Each candidate carries an author-confirmation comment, and the draft
header warns that copied wrong rules cannot catch themselves. Include ordinary
update candidates; explain omitted captured/transition forms. Full table
read/insert/update/delete declarations (and `write` for insert/update) cover
their corresponding effect in the syntactic audit summary; operation/column/
always assertions do not cover a whole table effect. Declared unproved or
refuted effects are still shown in the invariant verdicts.

### 10.5 Generated histories and production HTTP

Paired mutations require a stable privacy policy throughout execution: no
write to the protected table or any policy dependency, no insert/upsert/delete
(including implicit id minting), no implicit maintain/sequence/referential
writes, no assets with uncoupled ledger identities, and no opaque worker/native
context. Query logical payloads use the ordinary deterministic interpreter;
repeatability is an extra rejection check, never a proof of determinism.
Every excluded case is named unproved/not-covered. Owner-field patch authority
counts as effective access in missing-intent discovery and uncovered audit
entries, even if the table update rule denies; include the column and old-owner
predicate. Drafts explain that authority instead of inventing transition syntax.

Default test also explores short actual ordered mutation sequences from a
schema-valid focused fixture, then reads as the named ordinary viewers. The
record includes initial rows, each operation/viewer/typed argument/outcome and
the final ordinary read. Evaluate read intent in the actual post-history state,
never from a role's old grant. General `always` integrity can be refuted on
committed changed row images after an authored operation; no net image is used
to attribute per-write authority. Uncontrolled/implicit write authority still
needs boundary tracing before it can refute operation-specific write intent.
Enumerate declared personas/service seats and Cartesian enum/Boolean argument
tuples, with explicit caps and unvisited coverage; no passing bounded campaign
proves arbitrary histories. Temporal/captured/maintenance/asset-ledger fixture
histories remain not-covered until their complete replay inputs are present.

Signed-out challenges run in a private production `serve` child over the
actual schema, with no dev mode, fixtures or user credentials. Send unauthenticated
and forged-persona HTTP requests to every public query/mutation and verify
E_AUTH/401, plus closed development doors. Native/action/effect applications
requiring app-owned startup artifacts are named not-covered, not represented
by a partial schema host. Preparation/requests are bounded; kill/wait only
recorded children and remove the private temporary directory after process
exit. This qualifies auth admission, not role history or connected-device
revocation; STAGE retains ownership of staging/account provisioning.

The repaired 015 reference workflow records photo-backed placement/transfer/
adoption handoffs in the same ordinary mutation as custody changes; profile
provisioning and all pets/handoffs in its witness use authored operations.
Trusted seed is not used to manufacture the custody counterexample or repair.
General snapshot integrity still quantifies over arbitrary trusted ingress,
so the ordinary workflow test is not an all-ingress custody theorem.

A policy outside the bound rule/clock fragment is never dependency-free: paired
mutations decline it until dependency analysis of the complete retained AST
is available. The count-policy grant-before-read regression checks this
boundary explicitly. General aggregate integrity is interpreted over complete
validated raw snapshots for refutation only (count/sum and exact bounded
integer arithmetic); unsupported filters, time, captures and type coercions
remain unknown. This interpreter never supplies proof assumptions.

## 11. SEC2 reviewed checkpoint

The amendment and implementation received independent **READY** from fresh
Codex and Muse in round 5 at the reviewed source recorded in
`llp/reviews/3000.036.004-sec2.provenance.json`. All five rounds and their
verbatim outputs are retained. Earlier findings tightened dependency stability,
implicit id/asset entropy, bare-key provenance, owner-field discovery and
resource/error observation boundaries. No conservative blocker was converted
into a whole-exposure proof.

The native 20k and both-device 0–999 campaigns retain zero disagreements; the
Lean campaign retains exactly the four existing signature classes/counts.
The 150 original schemas compile with zero diagnostics and still have no
invariants: their generated operation runs are compatibility/exploration.
Installed-doc-only builder and repaired-lane probe evidence, full qualification
results and the remaining limits are indexed in
`snapback4/reports/20261018-sec2/` and the workstream report. This checkpoint
is not a zero-security-holes or publication capability claim.

### 11.1 Avoid duplicate concrete searches

Installed-doc builder measurements exposed minute-long repeated searches of
already-proved direct read/required-column components. Discharge those direct
searches with the existing reviewed component result, without promoting the
whole invariant or suppressing indirect paired/temporal/history/operation
challenges. For paired experiments, compute a fixed-point observer table set
from the protected table through maintained targets, inherited readers and
all table-rule dependencies. Skip authored operations mentioning none of that
set. This prunes finite experiments only; it contributes no proof assumption
and clears no blocker. Unknown/opaque observers retain their existing limits.

Proved ordinary insert/delete components also
need no duplicate direct witness search. Update/both-image claims are not
discharged by a next-image theorem. Before the unchanged bounded enum matrix,
try one row candidate pinned to explicit policy field literals (for example a
cancelled status). This candidate is not a proof fact: typed/default/final
validation, actual engine replay and policy-false judgment are unchanged.
Preserve every previous matrix sample; failed literal seeding only declines
that extra candidate.

For ordinary updates, prove the policy over both old and next images using
`update_rule_judged => policy.old_and_next`. Substitute an OldField with its
next-image Field only for id or an explicitly engine-enforced immutable local
column: every admitted update preserves those values. Never collapse mutable
fields, reference hops or their images. This is the same immutable-image law
used by the engine's once-judged update rule; it is not a new consistency
assumption about database contents. A named transition allowing only the next
owner cannot prove an old-and-next ownership policy. Owned-field bypass and
implicit writers retain their separate blockers and concrete searches. The
reviewed two-image component may discharge duplicate ordinary update/write
searches only where no owned-field bypass exists. Actual authored operation
matrices and unresolved observer obligations still run.

### 11.2 Faithful changed-image witnesses

The installed-doc builder found a misleading synthetic update witness: its
`row` repeated the pre-update row, so replaying that apparent unchanged patch
was refused even though the generator had actually changed status away from
the forbidden old value. Synthetic writes now read back the committed target,
record the actual next image and changed patch, and decline no-op/implicit-only
updates or a missing requested column change. The old image is recorded
separately. Under the existing both-image contract, a false old-image policy
can refute an admitted changed update even when the next image satisfies it;
that is not evidence the unchanged patch was admitted. The installed security
guide now states this distinction explicitly and routes per-operation role
authority to operation-specific declarations. Scope remains schema-valid
seed ingress plus synthetic engine operation, never ordinary app reachability.

Private maintained columns add their owning table, not merely their synthetic
maintain target, to the transitive observer set. Direct-search discharge must
not skip synthesized authored-operation assertions sharing the same source
site. Variant-independent unsupported operation preconditions (opaque body,
row-image policy, ambiguous writes and unstable dependencies) are checked once
before snapshot construction, with the same explicit unsupported reason.
Neither change reduces the previously executable argument/enum matrix.

### 11.3 Actual credential revocation admission

The private production HTTP campaign now authenticates through the schema’s declared guest or password method, confirms live schema admission, rotates that bearer, confirms successor admission, and logs out all sessions. It then requires E_AUTH/401 for both retired credentials at schema, changes, sync, probe, refresh and every authored query/mutation door. Credentials never enter counterexamples or logs. Schemas without ordinary identity and applications needing external startup artifacts retain explicit missing-coverage reasons. This tests connected HTTP admission after credential revocation; it does not assert that a disconnected device erased copied bytes, or establish current-role freshness without a sync round.

The campaign transport decodes HTTP chunk framing before parsing JSON: larger production schema responses use that framing. Truncated, oversized and malformed responses fail qualification rather than becoming a claimed refusal.

Final review hardening: require a distinct same-principal rotation successor and E_AUTH on the old token before logout-all, so mass revocation cannot mask a broken rotation. Declared Content-Length must match the complete received body; duplicate/invalid lengths and conflicting or unsupported transfer framing fail qualification, including a truncated response whose prefix is already complete JSON.

The private transport accepts the host’s declared-length or plain-chunked response fragment only: malformed header names/OWS, bare line breaks, signed/nonhex chunk sizes, unsupported chunk extensions and missing body framing fail qualification. On Darwin, the opened executable fd must match the device/inode of the VM region backing this process’s loaded Mach-O header (PROC_PIDREGIONPATHINFO); copy through that fd and reject a changing snapshot. A replaced pathname can never silently qualify a replacement image. The platform regression replaces a running child’s executable pathname before snapshotting and requires refusal. Unsupported platform/identity inspection fails qualification.

Both session responses must contain explicit nonempty string principal/token fields; missing/null/malformed identities cannot compare equal and qualify a same-principal rotation. Regression covers absent, null, empty, whitespace, non-string and unequal identities as well as an echoed bearer.

### 11.4 Complete compiled seat discovery

The finite cast includes service-seat literals from the compiled schema, authored operation IR and independently declared invariant policies. Table-rule-only discovery missed seats named only in operation require clauses or in intent. Extra service-prefixed data literals conservatively add actors; cast membership never proves principal reachability or creates a proof assumption. Existing casts remain included; larger bounded sequence/enum campaigns retain explicit unvisited reasons. Native/external worker artifacts remain outside this schema-only discovery claim. The matrix regression includes a table-rule-only seat, an operation-only seat and an invariant-only seat with nullable enum combinations.

### 11.5 Reuse pure invalid-world judgments

Within one paired snapshot variant, final-exists validation rejects the same committed fixture independently of the later operation/viewer. Cache only this exact typed structural rejection for that present or absent world, retaining every observer-specific unsupported reason. Never cache an operation result, policy judgment, allocation/storage/resource error or successful observation. Actual admitted calls, counterexample checks and repeatability replays are unchanged. This avoids repeatedly constructing the same invalid world during check; it does not turn missing fixture coverage into a pass. The existing social offline-receipts guard remains unchanged and measures the recovered authoring path.


## 12. SEC3 day-two amendment

Implementer: SEC3, 2026-10-19. Commission: day-two fix list 3/4/5/8.
REL5 owns release transitions and compatibility; MIG owns backfills and staging
clock control. This amendment changes security analysis, not runtime authority.

### 12.1 Column read intent

`invariant table.column read only P` protects the value, computations over it,
value-dependent counts/existence/refusals, copied values, assets and delivery.
It does not forbid observing an otherwise public row's existence independently
of the protected value. Binding validates the column and preserves its identity
in every verdict and audit. Effective payload authority is row read AND any
owner-private field gate. Pure projections excluding the field may eliminate
that payload path; predicates, group/order keys, derived values and copied
fields remain observations. Unknown flow stays unproved. A synthetic whole-row
read cannot refute a projection-only column policy: column counterexamples
execute an authored observer in two schema-valid worlds differing only in that
column, with policy false in both. Outputs must differ reproducibly. Maintained
values are recomputed; column-sensitive counts/existence are included. Separate
obligations name unresolved raw-probe, wire, device and opaque flows. A direct
column theorem never silently clears those obligations. Per-column audit
reports effective audience plus operation/derived observers, not only its type.

### 12.2 Reproducible campaigns and reachability

Generated seed ingress contains only authored base rows/fields. Never re-seed
maintained targets or engine-recorded fields. Generated lifetime samples are
live at the campaign clock; principal fields vary independently. Rejected
snapshots are recorded as unsupported, not successful attempts. Existing
fixture histories instead fork the complete SQLite store and asset ledger into
owned isolated memory stores; captures, deadlines, maintained values, lifetimes
and actual media identities survive unchanged. No source store is modified.
Temporary asset directories belong to Store and disappear on drop.

Actors include all principal values in fixtures. Required/optional references
range over fixture rows, not only the first. Short histories visit first steps
breadth first before extending them under a reported work cap. Read and row
assertions are checked after each step. Write/operation assertions judge only
actual committed changes, correct insert/update/delete arms and pre-write
policy state; ambiguous multiple writes, implicit effects or unstable policy
need executed-effect tracing and remain unsupported. A finite trace is never
an induction proof for always or arbitrary histories.

Every counterexample has a machine-readable origin: authored trace from trusted
fixture, trusted-seed-only, or synthetic operation. Only the first establishes
application reachability from the recorded trusted starting state and fails
normal check/test. Seed/synthetic witnesses remain refutations of all-snapshot
claims, visible with --all and JSON, without failing acceptance. Unproved
reachability is never asserted unreachable as a mathematical theorem. Check
loads the same fixture base for reachable histories as test, without HTTP or
business-case execution. A stronger witness must replace a synthetic witness
for the same declaration. --all exposes all witnesses and never changes which
ones fail. No unreachable refutation may print pass/ok beside exit 1.

### 12.3 Actionable authority advice

N_PRIVILEGE_ESCALATION identifies authored caller operations that write role
or group grants trusted by later rules while the effective admission does not
establish independent authority to confer that particular grant. Include
self-signup roles and transitions where a caller can confer a role they lack.
A trusted service seat or an independently authorized administrator may appoint
other roles; holding an unrelated ordinary role does not establish delegation.
Advice names the operation, grant and gate and points to guide staging's
operator first-admin recipe. It is advice, never an implicit runtime refusal
or a proof of malicious intent. Legitimate open enrollment can be intentional.

N_GRANT_OUTLIVES_ROLE requires an actually mutable/revocable current-role
population and a retained principal/grant branch lacking that role recheck;
cover read AND write branches. Immutable/static role populations do not fire.
N_EXISTENCE_ORACLE excludes public populations and caller-owned role lookups;
only an absent/hidden distinction crossing a narrower private audience warrants
advice. Every security note has a real source location and contributes to the
reported note count. Rule printing preserves connective precedence. Identity
429 responses include a conservative retry delay covering the rate window;
the existing limits and authentication semantics are unchanged.

### 12.4 Evidence

Qualification uses read-only copies of all ten wave-17 high lanes and their
spec-authored invariant sets, plus all 150 earlier schemas. Report caught,
partial and not caught separately; all-snapshot witnesses alone do not count
as a reachable detection. Preserve bad/fixed controls, note counts and source
hashes. The open qualification-gap ticket remains open for unresolved whole
proof/device/opaque obligations. No zero-hole claim follows from finite tests.


### 12.5 SEC3 reduction details

The direct column theorem is `(row_read AND owner_private_gate) => P` in the
existing three-valued kernel; deny-delete is never an admission for column
read. Whole proof still requires every observer obligation. This increment
uses dynamic column-world observers, not an unimplemented static dataflow
claim: pure projections can avoid a refutation, but do not acquire a proof by
absence of finite counterexamples. Census is existing point/scan/view/filter/
count/sum/exists, mutation return/refusal/copy, asset, sync, raw/derived/opaque
paths. Unsupported field flow remains unproved. Audit's `column_audiences`
maps every visible column name to its effective row-and-private-field rule;
operations and derived edges remain separately enumerated.

Column worlds use the same ordinary viewer, server clock and row id; the named
column has two different schema-valid typed values, and policy is false on its
respective image in each committed world. Every non-native authored query and
deterministic mutation is eligible; fresh ids, effects and incomplete/resource
results are declined. Compare typed logical data and authored refusal messages,
retain ordered arrays, repeat both observations to reject unstable outputs.
Rebuild maintained rows from authored inputs, never accept fabricated derived
or recorded fields. Required media substitutions without a coupled real ledger
remain explicitly unsupported. A primary observation from the exact trusted
fixture is a reachable observation; its synthetic alternate world establishes
value dependency, not reachability of an alternate application history. JSON
retains both worlds and explicitly states this distinction.

`AuthoredFixtureTrace`, `TrustedSeedOnly`, `SyntheticOperation` are the witness
origins (serialized in kebab-case). Status remains refuted for an all-snapshot
counterexample. Normal text labels seed/synthetic refutations non-failing and
hides their large witnesses; --all reveals them and does not change exit status.
Only authored fixture observations fail check/test. A reachable witness wins
over a synthetic witness for the same declaration. With no fixture, check uses
schema-only exploration and names missing application-reachability coverage.
Check discovers an explicit --fixture or project fixtures/; it uses an isolated
in-memory loader at the fixed campaign clock, never the development store.

Candidates sort by operation, argument value and principal. Enumerate bounded
Cartesian arguments including nullable enums and fixture references; interleave
operations for breadth-first first steps, then diagonal ordered pairs. The
512 first-step/512-pair and 1000-fixture-row caps are reported; no exhaustive
claim is made for unvisited combinations. Fixture asset directories are owned
by Store and removed on drop, including error returns. Histories judge direct
single-write net images only; multiple writes, dependency-changing and opaque
boundaries remain unsupported rather than fabricating write-boundary events.

The escalation advisory compares role privileges structurally, never by an
administrator role-name allowlist. Enumerate literals from a role enum or
role probes over a text roster; substitute each caller/assigned role into the
roster write gates and other table-effect gates. A possible ordinary assignment
that adds an effect the caller lacks warrants advice; explicit service-only
branches are excluded from this advisory cast, not from invariant proofs.
Literal assignment targets restrict the target set; dynamic values retain all
candidate roles. This is overapproximate advice: independent operation guards,
intentional enrollment and delegation still need specification review.
Grant-lifetime notes require a role/kind column with an authored update/upsert/
delete and a mutable role field; immutable seed-only populations are excluded.
Existence advice requires a private table lookup, an independent stricter read
policy and distinct later refusal; public and viewer-owned lookups are excluded.
Locations are exact column/rule sites where available, table sites otherwise;
the project-wide missing-intent note uses the first source's line 1.

Identity rate refusals on the existing identity routes use the existing
60-second WINDOW: Retry-After: 60, denied.retryAfterMs: 60000. This is a
conservative wait, not exposure of individual rate-key state. No limit changes.
Qualification inputs are ~/sb4-loop/wave17-repro/sec/<lane>/snapback/security.q
and read-only wave17 app copies; the report pins their hashes. The ten high
lanes are 006/011/013/015/019/021/027/040/045/048. Caught means an authored
fixture observation of the reported bad behavior; partial retains a relevant
note or synthetic witness with a missing affected path. Each of the eight real
highs is scored separately. All eight caught and no false refusals on 150 older
schemas is the target, never inferred from an incomplete run.


### 12.6 Disclosure and clock clarifications

A column observer mutation is declined if it can change the protected image,
policy dependency or an unresolved implicit writer before disclosure. A
pre-operation false policy cannot refute an authorized post-transfer return.
Column observers also run after committed history steps, preserving the
trusted initial fixture and authored prefix. All reference and principal
arguments use the same bounded fixture Cartesian cases; truncation of read
observer cases at 32 is named. Clock-only whole-row probes exclude columns.
Column tick coverage beyond the recorded campaign clock remains named.

All security fixture loading, probes, writes, paired deletions and policy
judgments use the same explicit campaign clock. Business tests keep their own
existing clock and store; security reloads trusted fixture files independently.
Raw policy probes respect both not-before and expire-at bounds. Direct delete
assertions judge removed pre-images against the stable pre-write state, never
surviving rows alone; ambiguous implicit removals remain unsupported.

Fixture forks copy already activated engine state without re-adopting a schema.
They use fresh entropy/minter and private assets, never shared live connections.
Ephemeral-hub fixtures require a separate isolated snapshot and are declined.
Structural privilege advice combines dominating safe operation requirements
with the actual insert/update/upsert gate and applicable owned-field patch gate.
A mutable roster alone is not enough for lifetime advice: require independent
current-role intent or a retained recipient column tied to a role literal
(judge, inspector, host, contractor, engineer; ordinary author attribution alone
is not a current-role contract). Deletion revokes even an immutable role field.

### 12.7 Stable judgments and direct payload witnesses

Unknown bound policy dependencies never authorize a mutation observer: such
column mutations require disclosure-boundary tracing. Pre-write assertions use
a transitive closure of maintained and cascade/set-null writes; a policy
dependency or target that may change implicitly makes the assertion unsupported.
The same rule covers insert, update, upsert and delete. Looped/opaque net images
cannot stand in for executed write events. Effective inserted authority includes
a defaulted role even when omitted from the source write.

An authored complete query returning a compiler-typed Row/Table or Page/Table
containing the protected row id is a direct payload witness at that query's
snapshot. Nested typed row returns retain their source-table identity. This
avoids inventing an invalid absent world by deleting a referenced parent.
Projected scalar/aggregate/refusal observations still require validated paired
worlds; a matching untyped id or value alone cannot attribute an exposure.

Check prioritizes actual fixture histories and column observers before searching
remaining synthetic counterexamples. It does not repeat the test-only operation
exploration matrix, which judges no additional policy. That matrix shares an
