    #[test]
    fn aged_bulk_progresses_when_the_bulk_thread_never_runs() {
        let host = Host::with_store(true, snapback4_core::store_port::AnyStore::memory().unwrap(),
            "table rows:\n  n: int\n  public\njob catchup():\n  for row in rows:\n    update rows[row.id] { n: 1 }\n");
        let shared = &host.shared;
        let job = lock(&shared.engine).enqueue_job("catchup", Default::default(), shared.now()).unwrap();
        // Healthy bulk gets no extra ordinary turn before its age threshold.
        let now = Instant::now();
        lock(&shared.maintenance).serviced = now;
        promote_aged(shared, now + BULK_AGE - Duration::from_nanos(1));
        assert_eq!(lock(&shared.maintenance).next, BulkKind::Delivery);
        assert_eq!(lock(&shared.engine).job(&job).unwrap().unwrap().chunks, 0);
        // No bulk thread exists. Three aged ordinary opportunities
        // still visit every bulk class, including the queued job.
        for kind in [BulkKind::Delivery, BulkKind::Recount, BulkKind::Job] {
            assert_eq!(lock(&shared.maintenance).next, kind);
            let due = lock(&shared.maintenance).serviced + BULK_AGE;
            lock(&shared.maintenance).serviced = Instant::now() - BULK_AGE;
            promote_aged(shared, due);
        }
        assert_eq!(lock(&shared.maintenance).next, BulkKind::Delivery);
        assert_eq!(lock(&shared.engine).job(&job).unwrap().unwrap().state, snapback4_core::JobState::Done);
    }

    #[test]
    fn stalled_bulk_admission_does_not_stop_an_ordinary_expiry_slice() {
        stalled_bulk(false);
    }

    #[test]
    fn stalled_bulk_engine_owner_leaves_the_gate_free_and_ordinary_admission_queued() {
        stalled_bulk(true);
    }

    fn stalled_bulk(holding: bool) {
        let host = Host::with_store(true, snapback4_core::store_port::AnyStore::memory().unwrap(),
            "table rows:\n  until: time\n  expire at .until\n  public\n");
        let shared = host.shared.clone();
        lock(&shared.engine).seed_at([("rows".into(), snapback4_core::value::object([
            ("id", snapback4_core::Value::Id("expired".into())),
            ("until", snapback4_core::Value::Int(1)),
        ]))], 0).unwrap();
        // A real bulk slice is stopped inside engine.background(), either
        // before admission (engine free) or immediately after owning it.
        let (entered, resume) = shared.engine.pause_next_background(holding);
        let worker = shared.clone();
        let bulk = std::thread::Builder::new().name("bulk-maintenance".into()).spawn(move || {
            crate::thread_priority::maintenance();
            bulk_slice(&worker, false);
        }).unwrap();
        entered.recv_timeout(Duration::from_secs(5)).unwrap();
        let (sent, observed) = std::sync::mpsc::channel();
        let ordinary = shared.clone();
        let timely = std::thread::spawn(move || {
            // Ordinary can enter its coordination slice while bulk is stopped.
            drop(lock(&ordinary.maintenance));
            sent.send(None).unwrap();
            let expired = timely_engine_work(&ordinary, |engine, budget| engine.sweep_expired_for(ordinary.now(), 2_000, budget)).unwrap();
            sent.send(Some(expired)).unwrap();
        });
        observed.recv_timeout(Duration::from_secs(5)).expect("ordinary slice blocked on the bulk gate");
        if holding {
            let until = Instant::now() + Duration::from_secs(5);
            while !shared.engine.has_waiters() { assert!(Instant::now() < until, "ordinary did not reach engine admission"); std::thread::yield_now(); }
            assert!(observed.try_recv().is_err(), "an exclusive engine cannot run two chunks at once");
            resume.send(()).unwrap();
            assert_eq!(observed.recv_timeout(Duration::from_secs(5)).unwrap(), Some(1));
        } else {
            // The regression: complete real expiry before bulk can run again.
            assert_eq!(observed.recv_timeout(Duration::from_secs(5)).unwrap(), Some(1));
            resume.send(()).unwrap();
        }
        timely.join().unwrap(); bulk.join().unwrap();
        assert!(lock(&shared.engine).store().rows("rows").unwrap().is_empty());
    }

    #[test]
    fn pacing_does_not_charge_time_already_spent_off_cpu() {
        let clock = SliceClock::start();
        assert!(clock.cpu.is_some(), "supported hosts provide a thread CPU clock");
        std::thread::sleep(Duration::from_millis(30));
        assert!(clock.consumed() < clock.wall.elapsed() / 2, "pacing charged the sleep as CPU work");
    }

    #[test]
    fn pacing_charges_atomic_overruns_but_cannot_suppress_aged_service() {
        for (elapsed, expected) in [(Duration::from_micros(10), Duration::from_micros(70)),
            (Duration::from_micros(250), Duration::from_micros(1750)),
            (Duration::from_millis(50), Duration::from_millis(100))] {
            let mut state = State::default();
            let now = state.resume_at;
            state.completed(now, elapsed, true, true);
            assert_eq!(state.resume_at - now, expected);
            assert!(!state.eligible(now, false));
            assert!(state.eligible(now + BULK_AGE, true));
        }
        let mut state = State::default();
        let now = state.resume_at;
        state.completed(now, WORK_TIME, false, true);
        assert!(state.eligible(now, false));
    }

    #[test]
    fn empty_kinds_repay_cpu_with_useful_work_or_before_idle_wait() {
        let mut state = State::default();
        let now = state.resume_at;
        state.completed(now, Duration::from_micros(10), true, false);
        state.completed(now, Duration::from_micros(20), true, false);
        assert!(state.eligible(now, false));
        state.completed(now, Duration::from_micros(250), true, true);
        assert_eq!(state.resume_at - now, Duration::from_micros(1960));
        assert_eq!(state.empty_pause, Duration::ZERO);
        assert!(state.eligible(now + BULK_AGE, true));

        let now = now + BULK_AGE;
        for _ in 0..3 { state.completed(now, Duration::from_micros(10), true, false); }
        assert_eq!(state.empty_cycle(now), Duration::from_micros(210));
        assert!(!state.eligible(now, false));
        assert_eq!(state.empty_pause, Duration::ZERO);
        assert!(state.eligible(now + BULK_AGE, true));
    }

    #[test]
    fn deferred_empty_cpu_keeps_each_capped_charge_without_longer_pauses() {
        let mut state = State::default();
        let now = state.resume_at;
        state.completed(now, Duration::from_millis(10), true, false);
        assert_eq!(state.empty_pause, Duration::from_millis(70));
        state.completed(now, Duration::from_millis(10), true, false);
        assert_eq!(state.resume_at - now, Duration::from_millis(100));
        assert_eq!(state.empty_pause, Duration::from_millis(40));
        let now = now + Duration::from_millis(100);
        state.completed(now, Duration::from_millis(50), true, true);
        assert_eq!(state.resume_at - now, Duration::from_millis(100));
        assert_eq!(state.empty_pause, Duration::from_millis(40));
        // 70 + 70 + capped(350) = 240 ms, paid as 100 + 100 + 40.
        assert_eq!(state.empty_cycle(now + Duration::from_millis(100)), Duration::from_millis(40));
        assert_eq!(state.empty_pause, Duration::ZERO);

        let now = now + BULK_AGE;
        state.completed(now, Duration::from_millis(10), true, false);
        state.completed(now, Duration::from_millis(50), true, true);
        // An empty-cycle check can race a timed worker's new 100 ms pause.
        // After 40 ms, 60 ms scheduled + 70 ms deferred must still be paid.
        assert_eq!(state.empty_cycle(now + Duration::from_millis(40)), Duration::from_millis(130));
        assert_eq!(state.empty_cycle(now + Duration::from_millis(140)), Duration::from_millis(30));
        assert_eq!(state.empty_cycle(now + Duration::from_millis(170)), Duration::ZERO);
    }

    #[test]
    fn slice_completion_preserves_an_empty_cycles_outstanding_repayment() {
        for worked in [true, false] {
            let mut state = State::default();
            let now = state.resume_at;
            state.completed(now, Duration::from_millis(10), true, false);
            // The aged worker starts a slice, then bulk flushes deferred debt.
            assert_eq!(state.empty_cycle(now), Duration::from_millis(70));
            let completed = now + Duration::from_millis(10);
            state.completed(completed, Duration::from_millis(10), true, worked);
            // Useful work repays immediately; empty work defers its charge.
            // Neither ordering can discard the 60 ms already outstanding.
            assert_eq!(state.resume_at - completed,
                Duration::from_millis(if worked { 130 } else { 60 }));
            assert_eq!(state.empty_cycle(completed), Duration::from_millis(130));
            assert!(!state.eligible(now + Duration::from_millis(139), false));
            assert!(state.eligible(now + Duration::from_millis(140), false));
            assert!(state.eligible(completed + BULK_AGE, true));
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn clock_drain_unwind_releases_background_work() {
        let host = Host::with_store(true, snapback4_core::store_port::AnyStore::memory().unwrap(), "table rows:\n  n: int\n  public\n");
        let result = std::panic::catch_unwind(std::panic::AssertUnwindSafe(|| {
            let _advancing = Advancing(&host.shared);
            lock(&host.shared.maintenance).advancing = true;
            assert_eq!(timely_engine_work(&host.shared, |_, _| -> Result<u64, RuntimeError> { panic!("ordinary slice ran during drain") }).unwrap(), 0);
            assert!(!bulk_slice(&host.shared, false));
            panic!("clock drain");
        }));
        assert!(result.is_err());
        assert!(lock(&host.shared.maintenance).eligible(Instant::now(), false));
    }
}

//! Bounded, read-only evidence from the store's own commit clock.
use snapback4_core::{Engine, RuntimeError};
use std::collections::BTreeSet;

const SKIPPED_PREVIEW: usize = 32;
const TOLERANCE_MS: i64 = 5_000;
const RECENT_COMMITS: usize = 64;
const TABLE_BYTES: usize = 4096;
const TABLE_NAMES: usize = 8;
const REPORT_ERROR_BYTES: usize = 1024;
// Reserve one MiB for the outer clock/work envelope inside the host encoder.
// The reply retains `schedules` and its fired/held partition.
const REPORT_BYTE_BUDGET: usize = (crate::serve::JSON_RESPONSE_CEILING - (1 << 20)) / 2;

// @ref LLP 3000.007#20.12 — inspect a fixed recent commit window, never application row values.
pub fn ahead(engine: &Engine, now: i64) -> Result<Option<String>, RuntimeError> {
    // Reverse primary-key traversal: no full scan, sort, row payloads or retained
    // historical stamp set. octet_length(column) uses SQLite record metadata;
    // unlike a text length/cast/substr, it need not load oversized payloads.
    let mut lead = 0;
    let mut tables = BTreeSet::new();
    let mut omitted = false;
    engine.store().visit_recent_commit_clock(now.saturating_add(TOLERANCE_MS), TABLE_BYTES as i64, RECENT_COMMITS as i64, |record| {
        let at = record.at;
        if at <= now.saturating_add(TOLERANCE_MS) { return Ok(()); }
        lead = lead.max(at.saturating_sub(now));
        let length = record.length.ok_or_else(|| RuntimeError::Store("commit clock record is missing touched length".into()))?;
        if length > TABLE_BYTES as i64 { omitted = true; return Ok(()); }
        let bytes = record.touched.ok_or_else(|| RuntimeError::Store("commit clock record is missing touched bytes".into()))?;
        match serde_json::from_slice::<Vec<String>>(&bytes) {
            Ok(names) => for name in names {
                if tables.contains(&name) { continue; }
                if tables.len() < TABLE_NAMES && name.len() <= 128 { tables.insert(name); }
                else { omitted = true; }
            },
            Err(_) => omitted = true,
        }
        Ok(())
    })?;
    if lead == 0 { return Ok(None); }
    let mut names = tables.into_iter().collect::<Vec<_>>();
    if omitted { names.push("additional tables omitted".into()); }
    if names.is_empty() { names.push("no table names recorded".into()); }
    Ok(Some(format!(
        "N_CLOCK_STORE_AHEAD: recent commit stamps lead the current clock by up to {lead}ms (latest {RECENT_COMMITS} commits; tables: {}); use a fresh store per offset test ({}), or restart with the same --clock-offset (or dev --resume-clock) to continue",
        names.join(", "), crate::dev_clock::isolated_command())))
}

/// UTC calendar text for Unix milliseconds: schedule boundaries are UTC.
pub fn utc(ms: i64) -> String {
    let (days, rem) = (ms.div_euclid(86_400_000), ms.rem_euclid(86_400_000));
    // Civil-from-days (proleptic Gregorian), exact for the I53 range.
    let z = days + 719_468;
    let era = z.div_euclid(146_097);
    let doe = z - era * 146_097;
    let yoe = (doe - doe / 1_460 + doe / 36_524 - doe / 146_096) / 365;
    let doy = doe - (365 * yoe + yoe / 4 - yoe / 100);
    let mp = (5 * doy + 2) / 153;
    let day = doy - (153 * mp + 2) / 5 + 1;
    let month = if mp < 10 { mp + 3 } else { mp - 9 };
    let year = yoe + era * 400 + i64::from(month <= 2);
    format!("{year:04}-{month:02}-{day:02}T{:02}:{:02}:{:02}Z", rem / 3_600_000, rem % 3_600_000 / 60_000, rem % 60_000 / 1_000)
}

/// A positive duration in the units `clock advance` accepts, rounded up to a second.
pub fn span(ms: i64) -> String {
    let seconds = (ms.max(0) + 999) / 1_000;
    let (d, h, m, s) = (seconds / 86_400, seconds % 86_400 / 3_600, seconds % 3_600 / 60, seconds % 60);
    let parts: Vec<String> = [(d, "d"), (h, "h"), (m, "m"), (s, "s")].into_iter().filter(|(n, _)| *n > 0).map(|(n, unit)| format!("{n}{unit}")).collect();
    if parts.is_empty() { "0s".into() } else { parts.join("") }
}

/// Each schedule's saved boundary, in declaration order.
pub fn saved_boundaries(engine: &Engine) -> Vec<Option<i64>> {
    engine.schema().schedules.iter()
        .map(|schedule| {
            let shape = engine.store().schedule_shape(&schedule.name).ok().flatten();
            if shape.as_ref().is_some_and(|shape| *shape != snapback4_core::value::digest(schedule)) { return None; }
            engine.store().schedule_boundary(&schedule.name).ok().flatten()
        })
        .collect()
}

/// Preflight is bounded before the clock or worker leases change.
// @ref LLP 3000.007#20.12.1 — only explicit execution enumerates all crossed windows; coalesced reports keep a bounded preview.
pub fn crossed_boundaries(engine: &Engine, before: &[Option<i64>], now: i64, held: bool, each_boundary: bool) -> Result<Vec<(usize, i64)>, snapback4_core::Refusal> {
    let mut boundaries = Vec::new();
    let mut report_bytes = 0usize;
    for (index, schedule) in engine.schema().schedules.iter().enumerate() {
        // JSON may escape every error byte; count that bound per schedule.
        report_bytes = report_bytes.saturating_add(2048 + 6 * (REPORT_ERROR_BYTES + 3) + 8 * (schedule.name.len() + schedule.target.len()));
        if report_bytes > REPORT_BYTE_BUDGET { return Err(crate::dev_clock::input("schedule report exceeds its byte budget; reduce the declared schedules")); }
        if held { continue; }
        let Some(old) = before.get(index).copied().flatten() else { continue; };
        let end = schedule.boundary(now);
        if old >= end { continue; }
        let periods = schedule.periods_between(old, end);
        if each_boundary && periods > (10_000 - boundaries.len()) as i64 {
            return Err(crate::dev_clock::input("--each-boundary crosses more than 10000 schedule windows; use a smaller duration or omit --each-boundary to coalesce"));
        }
        report_bytes = report_bytes.saturating_add((if each_boundary { periods as usize } else { (periods as usize).min(SKIPPED_PREVIEW + 1) }).saturating_mul(1024 + 8 * schedule.target.len()));
        if report_bytes > REPORT_BYTE_BUDGET { return Err(crate::dev_clock::input("schedule window report exceeds its byte budget; use a smaller duration")); }
        if !each_boundary { continue; }
        let mut boundary = schedule.next(old);
        while boundary <= end {
            boundaries.push((index, boundary));
            boundary = schedule.next(boundary);
        }
    }
    boundaries.sort_by_key(|(index, at)| (*at, *index));
    Ok(boundaries)
}

// @ref LLP 3000.000.000.001#11-wave-22-loop-repairs-dx6 — no silent successful advance behind retained schedule markers.
pub fn refuse_held(engine: &Engine, before: &[Option<i64>], current_clock: i64, now: i64) -> Result<(), snapback4_core::Refusal> {
    for (schedule, saved) in engine.schema().schedules.iter().zip(before) {
        // Equality is the already processed current window, not a hold. The
        // authoritative requested clock defines the window, never wall time.
        if let Some(saved) = saved.filter(|saved| *saved > schedule.boundary(now)) {
            return Err(snapback4_core::Refusal::new("E_CLOCK_HELD", "clock", format!(
                "schedule {} already processed boundary {}; requested clock {} is in an earlier window; next unprocessed boundary is {}. Nothing advanced. Advance {} to reach the saved window or use a fresh staging deployment; allowHeld:true explicitly accepts this hold. Never rewind saved boundaries",
                schedule.name, utc(saved), utc(now), utc(schedule.next(saved)), format!("{}ms", saved.saturating_sub(current_clock)))).guide("clock"));
        }
    }
    Ok(())
}

fn period(schedule: &snapback4_core::schema::Schedule) -> String {
    schedule.describe()
}

/// What each schedule did on one clock advance, and why one did not fire.
/// The core fires each schedule at most once per advance, for the latest
/// boundary, and holds it while its saved boundary is ahead of the clock.
// @ref LLP 3000#7-decisions-during-execution — missed boundaries fire once; this only explains them.
pub fn schedule_report(engine: &Engine, before: &[Option<i64>], fired: &[String], now: i64, current_clock: i64, held: bool, each_boundary: bool, port: Option<u16>) -> Vec<serde_json::Value> {
    let after = saved_boundaries(engine);
    // Read only bounded summaries: job args/cursors and full error payloads
    // are irrelevant to this report and must not be loaded then replicated.
    let runs = job_summaries(engine).unwrap_or_default();
    engine.schema().schedules.iter().enumerate().map(|(index, schedule)| {
        let (old, saved) = (before.get(index).copied().flatten(), after.get(index).copied().flatten());
        let current = schedule.boundary(now);
        let next = schedule.next(current);
        let mut entry = serde_json::json!({ "name": schedule.name, "target": schedule.target, "period": period(schedule), "fired": false, "firedWindows": [], "skippedBoundaries": [], "nextBoundary": utc(next) });
        if fired.contains(&schedule.name) {
            let end = saved.unwrap_or(current);
            entry["fired"] = true.into();
            let start = schedule.previous(end);
            let window = |boundary| serde_json::json!({"periodStart": schedule.previous(boundary), "periodEnd": boundary});
            let mut windows = Vec::new();
            if each_boundary {
                if let Some(old) = old {
                    let mut at = schedule.next(old);
                    while at <= end { windows.push(window(at)); at = schedule.next(at); }
                }
            } else { windows.push(window(end)); }
            if each_boundary {
                entry["reason"] = format!("fired {} windows: {}", windows.len(), windows.iter().map(|window| format!("{} to {}", utc(window["periodStart"].as_i64().unwrap()), utc(window["periodEnd"].as_i64().unwrap()))).collect::<Vec<_>>().join("; ")).into();
            }
            entry["firedWindows"] = windows.into();
            entry["periodStart"] = start.into();
            entry["periodEnd"] = end.into();
            if !each_boundary { entry["reason"] = format!("fired for the period {} to {}", utc(start), utc(end)).into(); }
            if let Some(run) = runs.get(&schedule.target) { entry["run"] = run.clone(); }
            // @ref LLP 3000.040#24-monthly-and-yearly-schedules — calendar periods count boundaries, not milliseconds.
            let skipped = if each_boundary { 0 } else { old.map(|old| schedule.periods_between(old, end) - 1).unwrap_or(0) };
            if skipped > 0 {
                entry["skippedPeriods"] = skipped.into();
                let mut windows = Vec::new();
                let mut at = schedule.next(old.unwrap());
                while at < end && windows.len() < SKIPPED_PREVIEW {
                    let mut item = window(at);
                    let mut args = serde_json::Map::new();
                    if let Some(program) = engine.program(&schedule.target) {
                        if program.args.contains_key("periodStart") { args.insert("periodStart".into(), schedule.previous(at).into()); }
                        if program.args.contains_key("periodEnd") { args.insert("periodEnd".into(), at.into()); }
                    }
                    item["command"] = format!("snapback4 run {} '{}'{}", schedule.target, serde_json::Value::Object(args), port.map(|port| format!(" --port {port}")).unwrap_or_default()).into();
                    windows.push(item); at = schedule.next(at);
                }
                entry["skippedBoundariesOmitted"] = (skipped - windows.len() as i64).into();
                entry["skippedBoundaries"] = windows.into();
                entry["reason"] = format!("fired once, for the latest period {} to {}; {skipped} earlier period{} this advance crossed (from {}) did not run: missed boundaries fire once. Run {} with periodStart/periodEnd for an earlier period",
                    utc(start), utc(end), if skipped == 1 { "" } else { "s" }, utc(old.unwrap_or(end)), schedule.target).into();
            }
        } else if held {
            entry["holdCode"] = "disabled".into();
            entry["reason"] = "schedules are held (dev --hold-schedules or --replay); a restart without the flag resumes at the next boundary".into();
        } else if let Some(saved) = saved.filter(|saved| old.is_some() && *saved > current) {
            let due = schedule.next(saved);
            entry["holdCode"] = "saved-boundary".into();
            entry["savedBoundary"] = saved.into();
            entry["heldUntil"] = utc(saved).into();
            entry["nextBoundary"] = utc(due).into();
            entry["reason"] = format!("held by the store: boundary {} was already processed and this clock {} is in an earlier window (restarting resets the process offset, not the saved boundary). One fire per boundary. Advance {} more to reach the saved window, or use a fresh staging deployment/store for an independent test; keep the same --clock-offset when continuing a test across serve restarts",
                utc(saved), utc(now), span(saved.saturating_sub(current_clock))).into();
        } else if old != saved {
            entry["holdCode"] = "initialized".into();
            entry["reason"] = format!("{} started at boundary {}: a schedule fires at the boundary after the first one it sees, next {} ({} from now)",
                if old.is_none() { "this schedule" } else { "this changed schedule" }, utc(saved.unwrap_or(current)), utc(next), span(next - now)).into();
        } else {
            entry["holdCode"] = "not-due".into();
            entry["reason"] = format!("next boundary {} ({} from now; schedule times are UTC)", utc(next), span(next - now)).into();
        }
        entry
    }).collect()
}

// @ref LLP 3000.000.000.001#10-wave-20-loop-repairs-dx5 — every declared schedule has one reported outcome.
pub fn outcomes(schedules: &[serde_json::Value]) -> (Vec<serde_json::Value>, Vec<serde_json::Value>) {
    schedules.iter().cloned().partition(|schedule| schedule["fired"] == true)
}

/// The report never loads full error/argument payloads from retained jobs.
fn job_summaries(engine: &Engine) -> Result<std::collections::BTreeMap<String, serde_json::Value>, RuntimeError> {
    let mut summaries = std::collections::BTreeMap::new();
    for summary in engine.store().job_summaries(REPORT_ERROR_BYTES)? {
        let name = summary.name;
        if summaries.contains_key(&name) { continue; }
        let mut error = summary.error;
        let truncated = summary.error_truncated;
        if let Some(text) = &mut error && truncated {
            let mut end = REPORT_ERROR_BYTES.min(text.len());
            while !text.is_char_boundary(end) { end -= 1; }
            text.truncate(end); text.push('…');
        }
        summaries.insert(name, serde_json::json!({ "id":summary.id, "state":summary.state,
            "rowsWritten":summary.rows_written, "error":error, "errorTruncated":truncated }));
    }
    Ok(summaries)
}

/// Startup lines for schedules the store holds: their saved boundary leads the clock.
pub fn held_schedules(engine: &Engine, now: i64) -> Vec<String> {
    engine.schema().schedules.iter().zip(saved_boundaries(engine)).filter_map(|(schedule, saved)| {
        let saved = saved.filter(|saved| *saved > schedule.boundary(now))?;
        let due = schedule.next(saved);
        Some(format!("clock     schedule {} is held until {} ({} from now): catch up to its saved boundary; next unprocessed window {}; `clock advance {}` or restart with dev --resume-clock",
            schedule.name, utc(saved), span(saved - now), utc(due), format!("{}ms", saved - now)))
    }).collect()
}

/// The dev clock offset that continues a store's own time: its newest
/// recent commit stamp (or saved schedule boundary) less wall time, never negative.
pub fn resume_offset(store: &snapback4_core::store_port::AnyStore, wall: i64) -> Result<i64, RuntimeError> {
    let commit = store.recent_commit_max_at(RECENT_COMMITS as i64)?;
    let boundary = store.latest_schedule_boundary()?;
    let latest = commit.into_iter().chain(boundary).max().unwrap_or(wall);
    // Whole seconds, rounded up, so restarting twice does not drift backwards.
    Ok((latest.saturating_sub(wall).max(0) + 999) / 1_000 * 1_000)
}

pub fn has_data(engine: &Engine) -> bool {
    engine.store().inspection_has_data().unwrap_or(false)
}

pub fn offset_line(offset: i64, running: bool) -> String {
    format!("clock     offset from wall time: {offset:+}ms{}", if running { " (lasts until restart)" } else { " (no running dev; inspecting against wall time)" })
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;
    fn engine() -> Engine {
        let bound = snapback4_lang::compile(&[("schema.q".into(), "table alpha:\n  at: time\n  public\ntable beta:\n  at: time\n  public\n".into())]);
        assert!(bound.diagnostics.is_empty(), "{:?}", bound.diagnostics);
        Engine::new_at(snapback4_core::store_port::AnyStore::memory().unwrap(), bound.schema,
            bound.programs.into_iter().map(|p| p.program), 100_000).unwrap()
    }
    fn seed(engine: &mut Engine, table: &str, commit_at: i64, row_at: i64) {
        engine.seed_at([(table.into(), snapback4_core::value::object([
            ("id", snapback4_core::Value::Id(snapback4_core::ids::mint(row_at, &mut snapback4_core::ids::Mint::default()).unwrap())),
            ("at", snapback4_core::Value::Int(row_at)),
        ]))], commit_at).unwrap();
    }
    #[test]
    fn clock_report_bounds_one_large_job_error_repeated_across_many_schedules() {
        let mut source = "table rows:\n  n: int\n  public 'fixture'\njob tick():\n  for row in rows:\n    update rows[row.id] {n:1}\n".to_owned();
        for n in 0..500 { source.push_str(&format!("schedule s{n} every 1m: tick\n")); }
        let bound = snapback4_lang::compile(&[("schema.q".into(), source)]);
        assert!(bound.diagnostics.is_empty(), "{:?}", bound.diagnostics);
        let mut engine = Engine::new_at(snapback4_core::store_port::AnyStore::memory().unwrap(), bound.schema, bound.programs.into_iter().map(|p|p.program), 0).unwrap();
        engine.fire_schedules(0).unwrap();
        let before = saved_boundaries(&engine);
        assert_eq!(crossed_boundaries(&engine, &before, 60_000, false, true).unwrap().len(), 500);
        let fired = engine.fire_schedules(60_000).unwrap();
        let message = "🧪\n\\".repeat(30_000);
        (match engine.store() { snapback4_core::store_port::AnyStore::Sqlite(inner) => inner }).test_support_conn().execute("UPDATE _jobs SET error = ?1 WHERE id = (SELECT id FROM _jobs ORDER BY created_at DESC, id DESC LIMIT 1)", [&message]).unwrap();
        let report = schedule_report(&engine, &before, &fired, 60_000, 60_000, false, false, None);
        assert_eq!(report.len(), 500);
        assert!(report.iter().all(|s| s["run"]["errorTruncated"] == true));
        assert!(report.iter().all(|s| s["run"]["error"].as_str().unwrap().len() <= REPORT_ERROR_BYTES + 3));
        assert!(serde_json::to_vec(&report).unwrap().len() < 2 << 20);
    }
    #[test]
    fn clock_report_refuses_before_the_host_encoder_limit() {
        let mut source = "table rows:\n  n: int\n  public 'fixture'\njob tick():\n  for row in rows:\n    update rows[row.id] {n:1}\n".to_owned();
        for n in 0..3000 { source.push_str(&format!("schedule s{n} every 1m: tick\n")); }
        let bound = snapback4_lang::compile(&[("schema.q".into(), source)]);
        assert!(bound.diagnostics.is_empty(), "{:?}", bound.diagnostics);
        let mut engine = Engine::new_at(snapback4_core::store_port::AnyStore::memory().unwrap(), bound.schema, bound.programs.into_iter().map(|p|p.program), 0).unwrap();
        engine.fire_schedules(0).unwrap();
        let before = saved_boundaries(&engine);
        let refusal = crossed_boundaries(&engine, &before, 60_000, false, true).unwrap_err();
        assert_eq!(refusal.code, "E_CLOCK_INPUT");
        assert!(refusal.message.contains("byte budget"));
        assert_eq!(before, saved_boundaries(&engine));
        assert!(REPORT_BYTE_BUDGET < crate::serve::JSON_RESPONSE_CEILING);
    }
    #[test]
    fn startup_hold_instruction_catches_up_without_repeating_the_saved_window() {
        let source = "table rows:\n  n: int\n  public 'fixture'\njob tick():\n  for row in rows:\n    update rows[row.id] {n:1}\nschedule hourly every 1h: tick\n";
        let bound = snapback4_lang::compile(&[("schema.q".into(), source.into())]);
        assert!(bound.diagnostics.is_empty(), "{:?}", bound.diagnostics);
        let mut engine = Engine::new_at(snapback4_core::store_port::AnyStore::memory().unwrap(), bound.schema,
            bound.programs.into_iter().map(|p|p.program), 0).unwrap();
        engine.fire_schedules(0).unwrap();
        let saved = 5 * 3_600_000;
        engine.fire_schedules(saved).unwrap();
        let raw = 1_234;
        let lines = held_schedules(&engine, raw);
        assert_eq!(lines.len(), 1);
        let line = &lines[0];
        assert!(line.contains(&format!("held until {}", utc(saved))), "{line}");
        assert!(line.contains(&format!("next unprocessed window {}", utc(saved + 3_600_000))), "{line}");
        let duration = line.split_once("`clock advance ").unwrap().1.split_once('`').unwrap().0;
        let delta = crate::dev_clock::duration(duration).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(delta, saved - raw);
        let before = saved_boundaries(&engine);
        refuse_held(&engine, &before, raw, raw + delta).unwrap();
        assert!(engine.fire_schedules(raw + delta).unwrap().is_empty());
        assert!(held_schedules(&engine, raw + delta).is_empty());
        let report = schedule_report(&engine, &before, &[], raw + delta, raw + delta, false, false, None);
        assert_eq!(report[0]["holdCode"], "not-due");
        assert_eq!(engine.fire_schedules(saved + 3_600_000).unwrap(), vec!["hourly"]);
    }

    #[test]
    fn utc_text_and_spans_match_the_calendar() {
        assert_eq!(utc(0), "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z");
        assert_eq!(utc(951_782_400_000), "2000-02-29T00:00:00Z");
        assert_eq!(utc(-1), "1969-12-31T23:59:59Z");
        assert_eq!(utc(1_791_468_000_000), "2026-10-08T14:00:00Z");
        assert_eq!(span(12_633_000), "3h30m33s");
        assert_eq!(span(86_400_001), "1d1s");
        assert_eq!(span(0), "0s");
    }
    #[test]
    fn resume_offset_follows_the_newest_commit_and_is_never_negative() {
        let mut engine = engine();
        assert_eq!(resume_offset(engine.store(), 100_000).unwrap(), 0);
        seed(&mut engine, "alpha", 3_700_500, 1);
        assert_eq!(resume_offset(engine.store(), 100_000).unwrap(), 3_601_000);
        assert_eq!(resume_offset(engine.store(), 9_000_000).unwrap(), 0);
    }
    #[test]
    fn commit_tolerance_and_largest_lead_ignore_future_application_values() {
        let mut engine = engine();
        seed(&mut engine, "alpha", 100_000, 1_000_000);
        assert!(ahead(&engine, 100_000).unwrap().is_none());
        seed(&mut engine, "alpha", 105_000, 2_000_000);
        seed(&mut engine, "beta", 107_000, 3_000_000);
        let note = ahead(&engine, 100_000).unwrap().unwrap();
        assert!(note.contains("up to 7000ms (latest 64 commits; tables: beta)"), "{note}");
        let note = ahead(&engine, 99_999).unwrap().unwrap();
        assert!(note.contains("up to 7001ms (latest 64 commits; tables: alpha, beta)"), "{note}");
        assert!(ahead(&engine, 102_000).unwrap().is_none());
    }
    #[test]
    fn recent_window_does_not_claim_older_commits_or_read_row_payloads() {
        let mut engine = engine();
        seed(&mut engine, "alpha", 200_000, 200_000);
        for n in 0..RECENT_COMMITS { seed(&mut engine, "beta", 100_000, 300_000 + n as i64); }
        // Deliberately unreadable images: metadata inspection must not deserialize them.
        (match engine.store() { snapback4_core::store_port::AnyStore::Sqlite(inner) => inner }).test_support_conn().execute("UPDATE r SET data = 'not json'", []).unwrap();
        assert!(ahead(&engine, 100_000).unwrap().is_none());
        (match engine.store() { snapback4_core::store_port::AnyStore::Sqlite(inner) => inner }).test_support_conn().execute("UPDATE _commits SET at = 200000, touched = ?1 WHERE seq = (SELECT MAX(seq) FROM _commits)", ["x".repeat(TABLE_BYTES + 1)]).unwrap();
        let note = ahead(&engine, 100_000).unwrap().unwrap();
        assert!(note.contains("100000ms") && note.contains("additional tables omitted"), "{note}");
    }
}

-stderr. Advance beyond the saved boundary's next window, keep --clock-offset

+`await host.advance("49h")` returns `{now, fired, held, maintenancePaused}`;
+`await host.now()` returns a timestamp. Numeric coercion of the report returns
+now, so arithmetic and `new Date(report)` still work; typed callers use report.now.
+The CLI `clock advance 49h --release staging` reports the same outcomes. Fired
+means enqueued: inspect the run state for parked work. Missed periods coalesce
+unless eachBoundary is explicit. Each held schedule explains its next boundary.
+
+Staging jumps preserve the remaining lifetime of live password/guest/full/read
+sessions by default. Expired or revoked authority stays expired or revoked.
+Use `await host.advance("8d", {sessions:"expire"})` to test session expiry
+explicitly (CLI --expire-sessions). Dev keeps its existing expiry behavior.
+Unplaced uploads and application deadlines still age; upload bytes after the jump.
+
+To exercise a mutation's own deadline check before due sweeps, use
+`await host.advance("22d", {drain:false})`, run the mutation, then
+`await host.drain()`. All background maintenance stays paused until drain,
+a draining advance, or restart; logical expiry and ordinary authorization still
+apply. CLI: `clock advance 22d --release staging --no-drain`, then
+`clock drain --release staging`. eachBoundary requires draining.
+
+Saved boundaries survive restart and never rewind. A blocked draining advance
+refuses E_CLOCK_HELD before moving time, naming the schedule and next window.
+Advance beyond that window, keep the cumulative --clock-offset when continuing
+across restarts, or deploy a fresh staging directory for an independent test.
+`allowHeld:true` (CLI --allow-held) explicitly accepts an already-processed
+boundary. Never repeat an ambiguous advance; inspect clock and queued work first.

# What Snapback 4 Does Not Do

Longer than the doing-list on purpose. Moving something off it means writing one
line naming what it unblocks and taking something off the doing-list in the same
change. Nothing comes off during slice one (LLP 3000 §3: the clock is four weeks).

## The bars

The bakeoff gates in [LLP 3000 §3](../llp/3000-snapback4.explainer.md) are the
bars: the loop bar, hub acquisition within 2× the measured floor, client bytes
under the competitor-anchored budgets, the six scenarios green in the simulator
on the hub fixture. Everything not required to pass them does not exist yet.

## Not building

- **A second authoring language.** Quarry, one spelling, copied from Snapback 2 (LLP 1004, LLP 1007 §4b). TypeScript is for seeds, journeys, effect bodies and the client.
- **Byte- and step-priced certification.** No closure, heap, output or step ceilings at `check`; the certificate certifies shape, uniformity, completeness class and prediction eligibility. Resources are metered at runtime (LLP 2000.000 §6).
- **A per-query result cache.** No range receipts, validators, halos, absence evidence, coverage spans, extent facts, held directories, fact integrity or swap journals. The client replicates declared partitions with one watermark each (LLP 2000.000 §7).
- **Engine-minted ids for client inserts, grants, ID slices.** Ids are client-minted, time-ordered, 128-bit; the engine mints for its own writes.
- **The `drain` protocol, follower-tab inbox rows, `defineItems`, `withHistory`, `mutationTarget`, `receipt.source`, `local.caughtUp`, `partial` reason codes.** The card (`packages/snapback4/src/contract.ts`) is the whole client vocabulary; `why` carries the rest.
- **`retain` as a receipt rule.** `until-revoked` and `delivered-history` survive as the client's leave policy on a scope tombstone.
- **JavaScript in the data plane.** Queries and mutations run in the Rust interpreter inside the SQLite transaction, and in the same interpreter on the client (host decided at week 3 by measurement, LLP 2000.000 §9). A *job* may be the app's own Rust, hosted as wasm through the interpreter's operations under the job's meter (LLP 3000.005, the Moves line below); a query or mutation may not.
- **An embedded JS engine for effects.** The data plane never calls out. `emit` writes the effect durably in the mutation's commit and an external worker holding a service token claims, performs and settles it over the wire (`snapback4/worker`); the four reference effects run on the builder's Node (LLP 2000.000 §10, decided 2026-09-13).
- **Committed generated code; an auth mode; a supervised bundler.** As Snapback 2 (`rules/NOT-DOING.md`): types by inference, personas not modes, `SNAPBACK_URL` is the client contract.
- **A TypeScript twin of the interpreter.** Retired by the author's ruling of 2026-09-13 (LLP 3000 §7): one implementation, in Rust, on every host — the core's SQLite under the native module, memory under wasm on the web with the host persisting each commit's changes. The web pays 312,924 B gzip before the diet where the twin's tier paid 16,842; the conformance obligation between two interpreters ends. Expo Go runs the online tier.
- **More than one hosted target, an admin console, media transcoding or thumbnails, push delivery itself (a worker's), cron syntax beyond `every N at HH:MM`, vector or relevance-ranked search (word-prefix search is in: `words(..)` and `matching`), federation, multi-region, device-to-device sync, at-rest encryption claims.** After the clock, on evidence.
- **General observability beyond `why`, `trace`, `logs`, `data`, `sql`, server operation latency, and bounded client subscription inspection.** The `sql` verb is read-only inspection of the developer's own store (LLP 3000.007 §8.8), never an application surface. Separately declared application SQL reads are admitted for increment D (LLP 3000.009 §6.2, §14.4; the 2026-09-16 Moves line below), not implemented by this inspection verb.
- **A guide corpus.** The compiler's facts, one language card and keyword cards, as Snapback 2; no freshness dates. Every card's Quarry is compiled by the suite and the language card is run, so a card cannot promise a form the parser refuses.

- **Partial union delivery, two group audiences, a public branch.** A union syncs principal-column branches and at most one group branch, each a whole disjunct of the read rule (LLP 3000.036.000.000); a branch with an extra condition, a second group or a `public` branch is refused with the rewrite, never partially delivered; service grants add no device audience (LLP 3000.007 §20.6). A union does not combine with delivered history, read-through children, synced or row-keyed views, owner keys, timelines, private field owners, acquisition windows or direct/inherited expiry on content or membership scopes.
- **Exact horizon maintenance.** The horizon bounds acquisition (a snapshot, a bootstrap); the log never evicts or back-fills to hold a device's group at exactly N rows. A local read past the acquired horizon by key says `complete: false`.

- **Clock expressions in rules.** A read rule compares with `=` and `!=` only; `.expiresAt > now` remains a mutation `require`. Stored lifetimes use `not before .col` for server-controlled opening and `expire at .col` for expiry. The engine publishes opening commits; devices receive no unopened payload. The supported compositions and explicit exclusions are in LLP 3000.036.003.
- **A jobs framework.** No priorities, worker pools or dead letters: one FIFO of runs, one chunk at a time, a refused chunk parked with its refusal. Actions, effects and scheduled actions carry per-operation retries, deadlines and cancellation, and a record per external step (LLP 3000.009 §5.2; the Moves line below). Missed period boundaries while a server is down fire once on return, not once per missed period.
- **Asset processing.** No transcoding, thumbnails, rungs or HEIC: the bytes are served as uploaded; JPEG, PNG, WebP and MP4 only; image dimensions and optional MP4 duration read from the header; MP4 dimensions are not extracted.
- **Search beyond word prefixes.** One tokenizer (NFC, lowercase, alphanumeric words), one index shape (`scope, words(cols), order.., id`), one read (`matching`): every term a prefix of some word, the first term's words merged as lanes, bounded by the meter in a uniform scope, at most 32 words in an admitted non-uniform scope. No stemming, no ranking by relevance, no phrase or mid-word matching, no per-language folding, no intersection index for the second term (it filters the page).
- **An identity provider.** Guests, password accounts, service seats, and sessions a service mints for accounts the application authenticated itself. No phone, OAuth, magic links or MFA in the engine: an application's worker verifies those and mints the session.
- **No multi-server presence, no presence history or last-seen storage, no broadcast event stream, no connection-bound rows.** `connected[p]` stays server-wide, counting held polls and their 35 s grace; a live query that may read it re-runs in the background about every 5 seconds to stay current (LLP 3000.018). Typing and viewing use short-lived, authorized ephemeral tables in one server process (LLP 3000.017); they never sync or decide durable invariants. A device does not know presence and says so.

## Process not doing

- **2026-09-28 — ordinary mixed search** (LLP 3000.028 §3.3, lane OS round 1).
  Admit the SDK's bounded merge of current server rows and certified Left images
  for the proved single time-ordered word page. This removes application-owned
  online/held selection for that shape. One server call per requested page;
  recomputation pays again from consumed positions. The coordinator shares the
  existing device read allowance. No durable search session, extra synced rows,
  new authority or additional allowance is admitted.

- **2026-09-28 — inferred current-scope word search** (LLP 3000.028 §3.3,
  lane OS). A single bare ordinary word page may derive the exact non-expiring
  membership audience for the existing compact server plan. This removes the
  requirement to repeat that audience predicate in this narrow server query.
  The compiler supplies a scoped words index when absent; it is an ordinary
  schema index, maintained on writes and on devices, with no extra synced rows
  or new authority. The device keeps its original bare scan. Round 0 left ordered composition
  and combined accounting outside its independent subset; round 1 above admits
  that bounded SDK composition. Durable search sessions remain excluded.
- **2026-10-12 — union sync audiences** (LLP 3000.036.000.000, workstream UNION, two blind review rounds). A table syncs to the union of principal-column audiences and one group audience; a device holds a row while any branch admits its viewer. What it unblocks: owner-or-team, buyer-or-seller and owner-or-staff tables offline for every reader, the shape three app farms asked for. Taken off: "one `sync` audience per table". Partial delivery, two groups and a public branch stay excluded (above).
- **2026-09-28 — explicit owner-key coverage** (LLP 3000.028 §3.4, Lane OK commission). A public window may opt into a compiler-owned, horizon-free principal key partition to answer ordinary own-key existence offline. Taken off: the exclusion of narrower platform key distribution beside one public window. General union audiences, full own-row replication and per-query absence caches remain excluded. The projection uses existing metered maintains, adoption and whole-partition publication; existing windows do not expand.
- **2026-09-26 — a live query keeps presence current** (LLP 3000.018). A 0.4.2 probe found an observed `connected[p]` reporting `fresh: true` while stale for over a minute, and a comparative builder polled around it. What it unblocks: online marks and presence-aware lists that stay current. Taken off: "a presence stream" as an exclusion for live queries; a presence API, last-seen storage and multi-server presence stay out. Under the author's standing authorization for reworks that make queries excellent (2026-09-25).

- **No drift registries, inventories, line-pinned diagnostics registries, claim digests or frozen-record gates.** Generated projections are built, not committed.
- **No gate bound to an exact commit; no push gated on a battery.** Five blocking checks in sixty seconds, run before push; everything slower on a schedule with bounded tickets.
- **No ceiling raised in slice one.** Budgets are anchored to a competitor's measured number and recorded once in the journal.
- **No standing panel** except the two blind reviews LLP 3000 decision 4 names (partition inversion; the meter's cut on non-uniform scans). The author explicitly commissioned the one-off LLP 3000.008 panel and disjoint Astra implementation lanes on 2026-09-14; its bounded disposition is recorded in that umbrella and LLP 3000 §7.
- **No new LLP number** without first extending LLP 3000 or LLP 2000.000; no spec without running code (`rules/RULES.md`: only implemented specs bind).
- **No second session on the core** during slice one; lanes take the periphery.
- **No test matrix as the primary harness.** The simulator is; real-browser and device witnesses cover only what it cannot reach.
- **No files over 1,500 lines**, including ones copied from Snapback 2. Split on
  the way in. The one exception is the package's published documents
  (`packages/snapback4/README.md` and its linked references): the rule exists to
  keep a *source* file reviewable, and the 0.2.25 calibration measured the cost of
  applying it to a document — splitting the README was that run's single largest
  scoring loss, because the builder then had four places to look instead of one
  (LLP 3000.007 §20.19). A published document is bounded by whether a builder can
  find one way in, not by a line count; the census that enforces this rule covers
  source, and says so.

## Deliberately worse

- No compatibility with Snapback 1 or Snapback 2 apps, packages or on-disk formats.
- No API stability before the clock; every publish is `0.0.x`.
- Sparse prose documentation; the diagnostics and the recipes carry the load.
- One hosted target, one platform binary at a time. SQLite remains the default store; Postgres as a production store is being built under LLP 3000.009.001 (Moves, 2026-10-20) and is not yet a supported deployment target.

## Moves

- **2026-10-20 — Snapback 4 on Postgres moves onto the doing-list** (author: "commit and push these things, then do your \"what i'd do next\" things, then get this working on postgres and measure it"; LLP 3000.009.001 and its children). Unblocks: the store-port extraction on SQLite (P0, including the `Committer` seam with the serial batch); the Postgres adapters for every durable-state family and `serve`/`deploy`/`doctor` over Postgres (P1), with store-held fencing, the declared HA mode and `BlobStore`; the optimistic committer, commissioned on 2026-10-19 and built after its execution stage is sized; the scale program of LLP 3000.009.001.002 with its raw-Postgres, Supabase and Convex controls on fleet machines; and a research note comparing replicated SQLite with Postgres for applications that outgrow one SQLite file. Taken off in the same change: the evaluation-only framing of the Postgres adapter. Stands: no publication or managed-service deployment authority, no lowering of Quarry to SQL, no SQL writes to managed data, one core owner. import { refreshSession } from "./auth.ts";
import { isReadToken } from "./read-token.ts";
import type { Client, Refusal, Session } from "./contract.ts";
import { readResponse, transportRefusal } from "./http-response.ts";

export const readOnlyRefusal = (code = "E_READ_ONLY"): Refusal => ({ code, family: "auth", guide: "read-only",
  message: ({ E_READ_ONLY: "this read session permits reads only; use a full session for writes",
    E_READ_ONLY_REFRESH: "read sessions cannot refresh; sign in again or narrow a full session again",
    E_READ_ONLY_DEVICE: "a read session cannot open a device; use the online read-only client",
    E_READ_ONLY_CREDENTIAL: "readOnly needs a server-verified read session, without a persona",
    E_READ_ONLY_UNSUPPORTED: "this server cannot verify read sessions; upgrade it before using readOnly" } as Record<string, string>)[code] ?? code });
export function refuseReadDevice(session?: Session | null, token?: string): void {
  // @ref LLP 3000.033#1.4 — token-based admission works offline and ignores forged scope fields.
  if (isReadToken(session?.token ?? token)) throw Object.assign(new Error("E_READ_ONLY_DEVICE: a read session cannot open a device"), { why: readOnlyRefusal("E_READ_ONLY_DEVICE") });
}
// Apply the same admission check to every device rotation, including a late
// successor. Refuse before adoption or persistence even if scope was forged.
export function refreshDeviceSession(...args: Parameters<typeof refreshSession>): ReturnType<typeof refreshSession> {
  return refreshSession(...args).then(result => { if (result.ok) refuseReadDevice(result.session); return result; });
}
export function validateReadOptions(options: { readOnly?: boolean; persona?: string; device?: unknown }): void {
  const code = options.readOnly && options.device ? "E_READ_ONLY_DEVICE" : options.readOnly && options.persona ? "E_READ_ONLY_CREDENTIAL" : undefined;
  if (code) throw Object.assign(new Error(`${code}: ${readOnlyRefusal(code).message}`), { why: readOnlyRefusal(code) });
}

const readiness = new WeakMap<Client, () => Promise<Refusal | undefined>>();
export const registerReadVerification = (client: Client, verify: () => Promise<Refusal | undefined>) => { readiness.set(client, verify); };
export const verifyReadClient = (client: Client) => readiness.get(client)?.() ?? Promise.resolve(undefined);

// @ref LLP 3000.033#1.4 — nothing passes this gate, including
// exported asset credentials, before the exact bearer/revision/store is verified.
export class ReadScopeGate {
  private accepted: string | undefined;
  private pending: { key: string; work: Promise<Refusal | undefined> } | undefined;
  private failed: { key: string; why: Refusal } | undefined;
  constructor(private url: string, private transport: typeof fetch,
    private current: () => { token: string | undefined; revision: number; store: string | undefined; closed: boolean },
    private accept: (json: Record<string, unknown>) => void, private signal: AbortSignal) {}
  private key() { const c = this.current(); return JSON.stringify([c.token, c.revision, c.store]); }
  get verified() { return !this.current().closed && this.accepted === this.key(); }
  get refusal() { return this.failed?.key === this.key() ? this.failed.why : undefined; }
  verify(): Promise<Refusal | undefined> {
    if (this.verified) return Promise.resolve(undefined);
    const key = this.key();
    if (this.failed?.key === key) return Promise.resolve(this.failed.why);
    if (this.pending?.key === key) return this.pending.work;
    const c = this.current();
    this.accepted = undefined;
    const work = (async () => {
      let why: Refusal | undefined;
      try {
        if (c.closed || !c.token) return readOnlyRefusal("E_READ_ONLY_CREDENTIAL");
        const response = await this.transport(`${this.url}/probe?scope=1`, { headers: { authorization: `Bearer ${c.token}` }, signal: this.signal });
        const json = await readResponse(response);
        if (key !== this.key() || this.current().closed) return { code: "E_AUTH", family: "auth", message: "the read credential changed during verification" };
        if (json.denied) why = json.denied as Refusal;
        else if (!response.ok || json.ok !== true || !["full", "read"].includes(String(json.scope)) || typeof json.store_id !== "string") why = readOnlyRefusal("E_READ_ONLY_UNSUPPORTED");
        else if (json.scope !== "read") why = readOnlyRefusal("E_READ_ONLY_CREDENTIAL");
        else { this.accept(json); this.accepted = this.key(); }
      } catch (error) { why = transportRefusal(error); }
      if (why && key === this.key() && !why.retryable) this.failed = { key, why };
      return why;
    })();
    this.pending = { key, work };
    void work.finally(() => { if (this.pending?.work === work) this.pending = undefined; });
    return work;
  }
}

  // Complete/release the original runtime only after capturing the crash.
  // Reopening uses independent storage copies and no original in-memory clock.
  f.release();assert.equal((await f.app.ready).ok,true);await f.app.close();
  const restored=await reopenCheckpoint(t,f,credentials,device);
  assert.ok(restored.client.now()<f.original.expiresAt);
});

test('failed App credential commit discards the provisional clock, including close',async t=>{
  const f=fixture(t,{reject:true});assert.equal((await f.app.ready).ok,false);await f.app.close();
  assert.equal(JSON.parse(f.values.get(f.key)).expiresAt,f.original.expiresAt);
  assert.ok(clockImages(f.persist).every(image=>image.offset<day));
  await reopenCheckpoint(t,f,new Map(f.values),clonePersistence(f.persist));
});

test('cancelled App opening never activates its prepared clock persistence',async t=>{
  const f=fixture(t,{held:true});await f.entered;
  const closed=f.app.close();f.release();await Promise.all([closed,f.app.ready]);
  assert.equal(f.app.auth.state,'signed-out');
  assert.ok(clockImages(f.persist).every(image=>image.offset<day));
  await reopenCheckpoint(t,f,new Map(f.values),clonePersistence(f.persist));
});

test('clock-save failure after App credential commit warns without rolling identity back',async t=>{
  const f=fixture(t,{clockFailure:true});assert.equal((await f.app.ready).ok,true);
  assert.ok(f.clockFailed());assert.equal(f.app.auth.state,'signed-in');assert.match(f.app.auth.why.message,/clock disk unavailable/);
  assert.equal(JSON.parse(f.values.get(f.key)).expiresAt,f.original.expiresAt+4*day);
  f.recoverClock();await f.app.client.query({kind:'query',name:'viewer'},{});await f.app.close();
  assert.ok(clockImages(f.persist).some(image=>image.offset>day),'ordinary device work retries the failed clock save');
});

## 11. Wave-22 loop repairs (DX6)

Commission: Charlie Cheever's wave-22 fixes #5, #6 and #8 (2026-10-22).
Implementer: Codex in sb4-b22-dx6. This amends §10, the staging clock of
LLP 3000.000.000.002 §4, supplied sessions in LLP 3000.036.004 §15.4,
and the starter application of LLP 3000.013.002 §2. SEC7 owns security advice,
intent, campaigns, upload recipes and the password/roles recipe.
This proposal is subject to the requested fresh Muse and Codex reviews.

### Session input and compatibility

Seeded records preserve the actual signup session's kind alongside its
principal, token and numeric expiresAt. They can be passed directly as Session.
Online createClient accepts a legacy incomplete session literal as token-only
transport credentials: its token must be nonempty; partial principal, kind and
expiry metadata never establishes identity, refresh timing or authority. The
server resolves the bearer; session() is null and there is no refresh timer,
as for the existing token option. Complete shapes remain strictly validated
and privately snapshotted. Local/device session input remains complete-only.
E_SESSION lists every missing/invalid field without values and gives the exact
one-line online repair createClient({ url, token }). An ISO expiry in a complete
shape refuses instead of creating a NaN timer. Restored full sessions retain
the existing restore validation and server expiry semantics.

### Advances, maintenance and retained boundaries

ClockAdvance remains an object reporting now/fired/held; valueOf returns now
for arithmetic, ordering and new Date(result). This is JavaScript numeric
coercion, not strict-equality compatibility; typed callers use result.now.

For classified staging, advance(duration) preserves remaining ordinary session
lifetimes by default. The core advances valid full/read session created/expiry
fields, read caps and recoverable mint receipts by the same checked delta,
in the same transaction as existing worker-lease preservation, before publishing
the new process clock. Expired, capped, revoked or superseded authority cannot
become live. Selection uses the authority kernel and bounded pages; overflow
refuses atomically. Existing action delegated sessions and supervised service
families remain owned by the worker-lease path, without double shifting.
Historical admission timestamps are evidence, not an ongoing cap; application
deadlines/backoffs remain business time.

Preservation includes SDK custody, not just raw HTTP credentials. A staging
response for the exact request bearer can publish authoritative session expiry
and read cap beside the same locked business-time/revision snapshot, obtained
through a detached store-identity/liveness-checked authority read. No bearer,
new authority, mint, rotation or refresh is exposed. Production publishes no
such metadata. A failed detached timing read suppresses the clock sample,
including streaming-final samples, instead of publishing advanced business
time with stale credential metadata. A client reconciles only its current
bearer's matching request URL/header and monotonically increases its live
expiry/cap before clock listeners run. Local/device clients await durable
credential custody before publishing or persisting their business clock.
Online clients keep a volatile clock; their existing session listeners may
persist custody asynchronously. Authenticated restoration still validates
expired metadata with the staging probe; no online durability barrier is implied.
Heartbeat final frames carry the same matching-bearer timing or unavailable
evidence as ordinary response headers. Reconciliation and the corresponding
local/device clock publication are serialized: durable credential saves are awaited
before publishing or persisting the advanced clock. A failed save leaves the
clock unchanged, retains dirty credential timing for retry, and surfaces as a
transport failure; rotation/close fences also suppress stale clock publication.
App preparation retains its existing private credential staging: prepared local
clock offsets remain non-durable, including on discard/close, until the actual
App credential commit succeeds. Only then may clock persistence activate before
the scope is published. A later clock-save failure reports a signed-in warning
and retries through ordinary device work; it cannot roll back durable identity.
The existing per-invocation response cutoff (LLP 3000.013 §6 and §12.7) also
spans implicit scope retirement's local credential cleanup. A scope-owned
reference count retains capture before teardown and through each scheduled
local credential task, releasing on rollback or close without waiting for an
auth operation or remote revocation queue.
Capture occurs synchronously when the response decoder validates a body,
before caller Promise continuations can cross that cutoff.
An invocation retains a body validated while live through settlement; a
completed capture owner cannot reopen its cutoff through another begin or hold.
Retention preserves a decoded body, not a stale authentication classification.
An E_AUTH refusal remains scoped to the bearer revision actually dispatched:
rotation supersedes prior and intermediate retiring-bearer revisions, including
when the response was decoded before rotation or arrives after cancellation or
a retryable refresh failure. Recheck that authority when consuming retained
responses. A successor already dispatched during credential persistence remains
current; its own refusal may sign it out. Sign-out alone does not supersede a
same-bearer refusal, and sent outcomes and business refusals retain their ordinary
invocation custody. Retryable refresh failure still permits a same-id retry under
the current credential revision.
Rotated/logged-out credentials cannot be restored by a late response. Client
clocks are isolated, so one bearer's response cannot expire another before its
own timing is reconciled. Read startup verifies before scheduling expiry;
an expired restored metadata image requires a successful authenticated read-only
staging probe with matching viewer/scope and live timing. Production/offline
without this evidence keeps the existing expiry refusal. The local constructor
reconciles bootstrap timing before applying a restored device clock's expiry
check. Tests retain actual read clients and restore them across their old
absolute expiry, compare two independent bearers, and exercise explicit-expiry
and production controls. These headers are staging timing evidence only;
ordinary authority is still checked on every server admission. Real elapsed time still consumes
credentials. sessions:'expire' explicitly tests expiry with the existing
business clock. Dev retains its existing expiry behavior. Production rejects
all clock controls and never calls preservation. Restart keeps the persisted
credential timestamps and drops only the existing process-local business offset.
This intentional staging-only simulated jump also shifts a read family's cap;
ordinary production read-cap immutability is unchanged.

advance(duration, {drain:false}) advances time and pauses background maintenance
before releasing the writer. This covers expiry sweeps, scheduled enqueue,
queued job chunks, asset collection, view recount and delivery maintenance,
so a mutation can exercise its own deadline check. Authorization and logical
row expiry still apply to ordinary queries/mutations. The pause lasts until
host.drain(), another draining advance, or process restart. drain() uses the
same authenticated endpoint with duration:'0ms', drain:true, advancing no time
and resuming normal coalesced maintenance. eachBoundary requires drain:true.
The HTTP report includes maintenancePaused; native CLI spells these controls
clock advance D --no-drain and clock drain. Failed/ambiguous requests are never
automatically replayed. A failed drain leaves its advanced time intact, its
report explicitly incomplete, and maintenance paused. Only a successful explicit
drain resumes it. drain() advances no time and safely continues existing queued
work/checkpoints; never repeat a lost advance to obtain that recovery.

A saved boundary is future-held only when it is strictly greater than the
boundary of the requested effective schedule window. Equality means that the
current window was already processed: report not-due, without consulting wall
time. Repeated advances inside that window and zero-time drains succeed without
allowHeld, including recovery of queued work after a failed drain completion.
Never enqueue the processed window again.
A draining advance whose saved future boundary blocks requested work refuses
E_CLOCK_HELD before clock, session or lease effects. The refusal names the
schedule, saved boundary, next unprocessed window and recovery duration to
reach the saved boundary from the unchanged process clock, not from the rejected
requested time. Relative recovery hints in accepted reports likewise use the
actual process clock, including when a disclosure floor is ahead of it.
A held report sets heldUntil to that saved boundary and
nextBoundary to the next unprocessed boundary. Catching up to heldUntil
reports not-due and never re-enqueues the processed window; reaching nextBoundary
fires once. Fresh staging storage and continuing with the original offset are
recovery choices; saved markers never rewind. allowHeld:true (CLI --allow-held) explicitly accepts a
retained boundary. Intentional drain:false pauses and dev --hold-schedules are
explicit holds. not-due/initialization remains a successful reported outcome.
Control authorization/classification is checked again under the actual writer.

### Upgrade advice and future formats

Advice is scoped to actual version transitions and each behavior's introduction
version. A fresh init/check is silent. Delivered stderr is acknowledged durably
for non-TTY callers too; baseline checks neither emit nor acknowledge advice.
The new upgrade helper retains warning stderr even under --quiet. Published
older quiet CLIs discard their check child's stderr without signalling this;
that historical capture cannot be distinguished from normal non-TTY delivery.
Advice from that old quiet path may therefore be acknowledged without display;
guide changes remains available. No ancestor
process inspection or script mutation is introduced.

The bounded candidate scan covers partial session literals and numeric advance
uses, explicit persistent startDev calls and data --json consumers. Explicit
nearby refusal assertions do not become dev-door warnings. Candidate paths,
never source or credentials, are printed; incomplete scans remain disclosed.
Future known-family store formats refuse with 'a newer Snapback (FORMAT)'.
Read-only SQL inspection validates the format before exposing rows and exits
nonzero on refusal. Already published old binaries cannot be repaired.

Both list starters render through the packaged ReadState. Proven absence and

This is a public same-origin test channel, not a secret or an authentication

Whitespace normalization collapses runs and trims both ends; case is preserved,

explicit substring strings are case-insensitive and regex follows its pattern/flags.
String matching stays exact by default; substring is explicit, never a silent
fallback. A composed label cannot make an unrelated sibling count as success.
